content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.224/57410ae27030c388fa94d523bec9ab6b/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Local dashboard for the E36 DME.

Runs entirely on stdlib plus pyserial -- no framework, no CDN, nothing to
install. Everything is served from localhost.

The design constraint that shapes this: the K-line is a single serial port and
only one thing may own it. So exactly one background thread holds the ECU
session and publishes the latest sample into a shared dict; HTTP handlers only
ever read that dict. Browser requests never touch the port.

It is also useful with no car attached -- captured CSV logs and saved fault
snapshots render fine offline, which is most of what you want when reviewing
a session afterwards.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

from .faults import decode as decode_faults
from .kline import KLineError
from .live import LiveReader
from .sensors import CORE_SENSORS

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STATIC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "static", "dashboard.html")


class Poller(threading.Thread):
    """Owns the ECU session and republishes the latest sample."""

    def __init__(self, port: str, address: int, interval: float, enabled: bool) -> None:
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.port = port
        self.address = address
        self.interval = interval
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.state: dict = {
            "connected": False,
            "status": "sin ECU" if enabled else "modo sin conexión",
            "live": None,
            "ecu_id": None,
            "faults": [],
            "faults_note": "",
        }
        self._stop = threading.Event()

    def publish(self, **kw) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.state.update(kw)

    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return dict(self.state)

    def run(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            self._offline_faults()
            return
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                self._session()
            except (KLineError, OSError) as exc:
                log.debug("session failed: %s", exc)
                self.publish(connected=False, live=None,
                             status=f"sin ECU ({type(exc).__name__})")
                self._offline_faults()
                self._stop.wait(6.0)

    def _session(self) -> None:
        reader = LiveReader(self.port, address=self.address)
        with reader:
            session = reader._session
            ids = [s.decode("ascii", "replace").strip() for s in session.id_strings]
            self.publish(connected=True, status="conectada", ecu_id=ids)

            # Read fault memory once per session rather than every tick -- it
            # changes rarely and each read costs a full round trip.
            try:
                raw = b"".join(session.read_fault_codes())
                self.publish(faults=self._encode(decode_faults(raw)),

"""Local dashboard for the E36 DME.

Runs entirely on stdlib plus pyserial -- no framework, no CDN, nothing to
install. Everything is served from localhost.

The design constraint that shapes this: the K-line is a single serial port and
only one thing may own it. So exactly one background thread holds the ECU
session and publishes the latest sample into a shared dict; HTTP handlers only
ever read that dict. Browser requests never touch the port.

It is also useful with no car attached -- captured CSV logs and saved fault
snapshots render fine offline, which is most of what you want when reviewing
a session afterwards.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

from .faults import decode as decode_faults
from .kline import KLineError
from .live import LiveReader
from .sensors import CORE_SENSORS

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STATIC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "static", "dashboard.html")


class Poller(threading.Thread):
    """Owns the ECU session and republishes the latest sample."""

    def __init__(self, port: str, address: int, interval: float, enabled: bool) -> None:
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.port = port
        self.address = address
        self.interval = interval
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.state: dict = {
            "connected": False,
            "status": "sin ECU" if enabled else "modo sin conexión",
            "live": None,
            "ecu_id": None,
            "faults": [],
            "faults_note": "",
        }
        self._stop = threading.Event()

    def publish(self, **kw) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.state.update(kw)

    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return dict(self.state)

    def run(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            self._offline_faults()
            return
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                self._session()
            except (KLineError, OSError) as exc:
                log.debug("session failed: %s", exc)
                self.publish(connected=False, live=None,
                             status=f"sin ECU ({type(exc).__name__})")
                self._offline_faults()
                self._stop.wait(6.0)

    def _session(self) -> None:
        reader = LiveReader(self.port, address=self.address)
        with reader:
            session = reader._session
            ids = [s.decode("ascii", "replace").strip() for s in session.id_strings]
            self.publish(connected=True, status="conectada", ecu_id=ids)

            # Read fault memory once per session rather than every tick -- it
            # changes rarely and each read costs a full round trip.
            try:
                raw = b"".join(session.read_fault_codes())
                self.publish(faults=self._encode(decode_faults(raw)),

            except KLineError as exc:
                log.debug("fault read failed: %s", exc)

            while not self._stop.is_set():
                sample = reader.sample()

                    raise KLineError("perdimos la ECU")
                values = {s.name: round(s.scale(sample[s.name]), 3)
                          for s in CORE_SENSORS}
                self.publish(connected=True, live=values, status="conectada")
                self._stop.wait(self.interval)

    def _offline_faults(self) -> None:
        """With no ECU, fall back to the most recent saved snapshot."""
        if self.state.get("faults"):
            return

        for path in reversed(files):

                    data = json.load(fh)
                if "codes" in data:
                    self.publish(faults=data["codes"],
                                 faults_note=f"de {os.path.basename(path)}")
                    return
            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
                continue

    @staticmethod
    def _encode(codes) -> list[dict]:
        return [{
            "number": c.number, "description": c.description,
            "condition": c.condition, "conditions": c.conditions,
            "frequency": c.frequency, "rpm": c.rpm,
        } for c in codes]

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args) -> None:  # keep the console clean
            pass

        def _send(self, body: bytes, ctype: str) -> None:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def _json(self, obj) -> None:
            self._send(json.dumps(obj).encode(), "application/json")

        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            query = parse_qs(route.query)

            if route.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
                with open(STATIC, "rb") as fh:
                    self._send(fh.read(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")

            elif route.path == "/api/state":
                self._json(poller.snapshot())

            elif route.path == "/api/logs":
                self._json(sorted(glob.glob("*.csv"), reverse=True))

            elif route.path == "/api/log":
                name = (query.get("name") or [""])[0]
                # Only serve CSVs from the working directory -- no traversal.
                if not name or os.path.basename(name) != name or not name.endswith(".csv"):
                    self._json([])
                    return
                try:

                        self._json(list(csv.DictReader(fh)))
                except OSError:
                    self._json([])
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

    return Handler


def serve(port: str, http_port: int = 8036, address: int = 0x10,
          interval: float = 1.0, live: bool = True) -> None:
    poller = Poller(port, address, interval, enabled=live)
    poller.start()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", http_port), make_handler(poller))
    print(f"\n  Dashboard:  http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}")
    print(f"  ECU:        {'polling ' + port if live else 'desactivado (--no-live)'}")
    print("  Ctrl-C para salir\n")
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\ncerrando…")
    finally:
        poller.stop()
        server.server_close()


Abre en **http://127.0.0.1:8036** — todo local, sin dependencias nuevas, sin internet. Solo stdlib de Python más pyserial, que ya tenías.

**Funciona ahora mismo sin el auto**, que es lo que probé: te muestra los dos códigos de falla con su severidad y las tres capturas de hoy en gráficos. Cuando conectes el cable con el contacto puesto, arranca a mostrar valores en vivo automáticamente. Si no encuentra la ECU, cae solo a modo offline sin romperse.

**Decisiones de diseño que vale la pena que sepas:**

**Un gráfico por sensor, no todos juntos.** Régimen (~900), refrigerante (~50 °C), batería (13.5 V) y carga (2.8 ms) viven en escalas totalmente distintas. Meterlos en un mismo gráfico obligaría a dos ejes Y, que es la peor cosa que se le puede hacer a una lectura — hace que dos series parezcan cruzarse cuando no tienen nada que ver. Cada uno con su eje propio.

"""Local dashboard for the E36 DME, with actions.

Runs entirely on stdlib plus pyserial -- no framework, no CDN, nothing to
install. Everything is served from localhost.

The design constraint that shapes all of this: the K-line is a single serial
port and only one thing may own it at a time. So there is exactly ONE thread
that ever touches serial. It maintains the live session, and between samples it
drains an action queue. HTTP handlers never open the port -- they enqueue work
and poll for the result. That is why recording, fault snapshots and the DS2
probe can coexist with live polling without fighting over the device.

It is also useful with no car attached: captured CSV logs and saved fault
snapshots render fine offline, which is most of what you want when reviewing a
session afterwards.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import json
import logging
import os
import queue
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

from .ds2 import COMMON_ADDRESSES as DS2_ADDRESSES
from .ds2 import DS2, DS2Error
from .faults import decode as decode_faults
from .kline import KLineError
from .live import LiveReader
from .sensors import CORE_SENSORS
from .snapshot import Snapshot

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STATIC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "static", "dashboard.html")
MAX_EVENTS = 40


def stamp() -> str:
    return datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")


class Poller(threading.Thread):
    """The only thread that touches the serial port."""

    def __init__(self, port: str, address: int, interval: float, enabled: bool) -> None:
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.port = port
        self.address = address
        self.interval = interval
        self.enabled = enabled

        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.actions: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()
        self._stop = threading.Event()

        self._reader: LiveReader | None = None
        self._csv_fh = None
        self._csv_writer = None
        self._recording_name = ""
        self._record_started = 0.0
        self._record_rows = 0

        self.state: dict = {
            "connected": False,
            "status": "sin ECU" if enabled else "modo sin conexión",
            "live": None,
            "ecu_id": None,
            "faults": [],
            "faults_note": "",
            "recording": None,
            "events": [],
            "busy": "",
        }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- publishing

    def publish(self, **kw) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.state.update(kw)

    def event(self, text: str, kind: str = "info") -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.state["events"] = (
                [{"t": stamp(), "text": text, "kind": kind}] + self.state["events"]
            )[:MAX_EVENTS]

    def snapshot_state(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return dict(self.state)

    def submit(self, action: str, params: dict) -> None:
        self.actions.put((action, params))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------- main loop

    def run(self) -> None:
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            self._drain_actions()
            if not self.enabled:
                self._offline_faults()
                self._stop.wait(0.4)
                continue
            try:
                self._session()
            except (KLineError, OSError) as exc:
                log.debug("session ended: %s", exc)
                self._teardown()
                self.publish(connected=False, live=None,
                             status=f"sin ECU ({type(exc).__name__})")
                self._offline_faults()
                self._stop.wait(5.0)

    def _session(self) -> None:
        self._reader = LiveReader(self.port, address=self.address)
        self._reader._open()
        session = self._reader._session
        ids = [s.decode("ascii", "replace").strip() for s in session.id_strings]
        self.publish(connected=True, status="conectada", ecu_id=ids)
        self.event("ECU conectada en 0x%02X" % self.address, "good")
        self._read_faults()

        while not self._stop.is_set():
            self._drain_actions()
            if self._reader is None:      # an action tore the session down
                return
            sample = self._reader.sample()
            if sample is None:
                raise KLineError("se perdió la ECU")
            values = {s.name: round(s.scale(sample[s.name]), 3) for s in CORE_SENSORS}
            self.publish(connected=True, live=values, status="conectada")
            self._write_row(values)
            self._stop.wait(self.interval)

    def _teardown(self) -> None:
        if self._reader is not None:
            self._reader._close()
            self._reader = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- actions

    def _drain_actions(self) -> None:
        while True:
            try:
                action, params = self.actions.get_nowait()
            except queue.Empty:
                return
            handler = getattr(self, f"_do_{action}", None)
            if handler is None:
                self.event(f"acción desconocida: {action}", "bad")
                continue
            self.publish(busy=action)
            try:
                handler(params)
            except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001
                log.debug("action %s failed: %s", action, exc)
                self.event(f"{action} falló: {exc}", "bad")
            finally:
                self.publish(busy="")

    def _do_record_start(self, params: dict) -> None:
        if self._csv_writer is not None:
            self.event("ya se está grabando", "warn")
            return
        name = params.get("name") or f"rec_{datetime.now():%H%M%S}.csv"
        if not name.endswith(".csv"):
            name += ".csv"
        name = os.path.basename(name)
        self._csv_fh = open(name, "w", newline="")
        self._csv_writer = csv.writer(self._csv_fh)
        self._csv_writer.writerow(["timestamp", "elapsed_s"] + [s.name for s in CORE_SENSORS])
        self._recording_name = name
        self._record_started = time.monotonic()
        self._record_rows = 0
        self.publish(recording={"name": name, "rows": 0})
        self.event(f"grabando en {name}", "good")

    def _do_record_stop(self, params: dict) -> None:
        if self._csv_writer is None:
            return
        self._csv_fh.close()
        self._csv_writer = None
        self._csv_fh = None
        self.publish(recording=None)
        self.event(f"grabación detenida: {self._recording_name} "
                   f"({self._record_rows} muestras)", "good")

    def _write_row(self, values: dict) -> None:
        if self._csv_writer is None:
            return
        self._csv_writer.writerow(
            [datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds"),
             f"{time.monotonic() - self._record_started:.3f}"]
            + [values[s.name] for s in CORE_SENSORS]
        )
        self._csv_fh.flush()
        self._record_rows += 1
        self.publish(recording={"name": self._recording_name, "rows": self._record_rows})

    def _do_refresh_faults(self, params: dict) -> None:
        if self._reader is None:
            self.event("sin ECU: no se pueden releer fallas", "warn")
            return
        self._read_faults()

    def _read_faults(self) -> None:
        try:
            raw = b"".join(self._reader._session.read_fault_codes())
        except KLineError as exc:
            self.event(f"lectura de fallas falló: {exc}", "bad")
            return
        codes = decode_faults(raw)
        self.publish(faults=self._encode(codes), faults_note="leído de la ECU")
        self.event(f"{len(codes)} código(s) leídos de la ECU", "good")
        self._last_raw = raw

    def _do_snapshot(self, params: dict) -> None:
        raw = getattr(self, "_last_raw", None)
        if raw is None:
            self.event("no hay lectura de fallas para guardar", "warn")
            return
        os.makedirs("snapshots", exist_ok=True)
        name = params.get("note") or "snapshot"
        path = os.path.join("snapshots", f"{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}.json")
        Snapshot.capture(raw, note=name).save(path)
        self.event(f"snapshot guardado: {path}", "good")

    def _do_ds2_scan(self, params: dict) -> None:
        """Probe DS2 modules -- needs the port, so the KWP71 session steps aside.

        DS2 uses even parity and no init, so it cannot share a session with the
        KWP71 DME. We close cleanly, scan, and let the main loop rebuild.
        """
        was_live = self._reader is not None
        self._teardown()
        self.publish(connected=False, live=None, status="buscando módulos DS2…")
        self.event("buscando módulos DS2 (EGS, ABS…)", "info")

        hits = []
        try:
            with DS2(self.port, timeout=1.0) as bus:
                for addr in DS2_ADDRESSES:
                    reply = bus.probe(addr)
                    if reply is None:
                        continue
                    text = reply.decode("ascii", "replace").strip()
                    hits.append({"address": f"0x{addr:02X}", "id": text,
                                 "raw": reply.hex(" ")})
                    self.event(f"módulo en 0x{addr:02X}: {text or reply.hex(' ')}", "good")
                    try:
                        faults = bus.read_faults(addr)
                        self.event(f"  fallas 0x{addr:02X}: {faults.hex(' ')}", "info")
                        hits[-1]["faults"] = faults.hex(" ")
                    except DS2Error as exc:
                        self.event(f"  sin memoria de fallas en 0x{addr:02X}: {exc}", "warn")
                    time.sleep(0.1)
        except Exception as exc:                          # noqa: BLE001
            self.event(f"escaneo DS2 falló: {exc}", "bad")

        if not hits:
            self.event("ningún módulo DS2 respondió", "warn")
        self.publish(ds2=hits)
        if not was_live:
            self.publish(status="modo sin conexión" if not self.enabled else "sin ECU")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- offline

    def _offline_faults(self) -> None:
        if self.state.get("faults"):
            return
        files = sorted(glob.glob("*.json")) + sorted(glob.glob("snapshots/*.json"))
        for path in reversed(files):
            try:
                with open(path) as fh:
                    data = json.load(fh)
                if "codes" in data:
                    self.publish(faults=data["codes"],
                                 faults_note=f"de {os.path.basename(path)}")
                    return
            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
                continue

    @staticmethod
    def _encode(codes) -> list[dict]:
        return [{
            "number": c.number, "description": c.description,
            "condition": c.condition, "conditions": c.conditions,
            "frequency": c.frequency, "rpm": c.rpm,
        } for c in codes]

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        self._do_record_stop({})


def make_handler(poller: Poller):
    ALLOWED = {"record_start", "record_stop", "refresh_faults", "snapshot", "ds2_scan"}

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args) -> None:
            pass

        def _send(self, body: bytes, ctype: str) -> None:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def _json(self, obj) -> None:
            self._send(json.dumps(obj).encode(), "application/json")

        def do_POST(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            if route.path != "/api/action":
                self.send_error(404)
                return
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            try:
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            except ValueError:
                self._json({"ok": False, "error": "json inválido"})
                return
            action = body.get("action", "")
            if action not in ALLOWED:
                self._json({"ok": False, "error": f"acción no permitida: {action}"})
                return
            poller.submit(action, body.get("params") or {})
            self._json({"ok": True, "queued": action})

        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            query = parse_qs(route.query)

            if route.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
                with open(STATIC, "rb") as fh:
                    self._send(fh.read(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")

            elif route.path == "/api/state":
                self._json(poller.snapshot_state())

            elif route.path == "/api/logs":
                self._json(sorted(glob.glob("*.csv"), reverse=True))

            elif route.path == "/api/log":
                name = (query.get("name") or [""])[0]
                # Only serve CSVs from the working directory -- no traversal.
                if not name or os.path.basename(name) != name or not name.endswith(".csv"):
                    self._json([])
                    return
                try:
                    with open(name, newline="") as fh:
                        self._json(list(csv.DictReader(fh)))
                except OSError:
                    self._json([])
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

    return Handler


def serve(port: str, http_port: int = 8036, address: int = 0x10,
          interval: float = 1.0, live: bool = True) -> None:
    poller = Poller(port, address, interval, enabled=live)
    poller.start()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", http_port), make_handler(poller))
    print(f"\n  Dashboard:  http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}")
    print(f"  ECU:        {'polling ' + port if live else 'desactivado (--no-live)'}")
    print("  Ctrl-C para salir\n")
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\ncerrando…")
    finally:
        poller.stop()
        server.server_close()

        self._last_raw = raw

    def _do_snapshot(self, params: dict) -> None:
        raw = getattr(self, "_last_raw", None)
        if raw is None:
            self.event("no hay lectura de fallas para guardar", "warn")
            return
        os.makedirs("snapshots", exist_ok=True)
        name = params.get("note") or "snapshot"
        path = os.path.join("snapshots", f"{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}.json")
        Snapshot.capture(raw, note=name).save(path)
        self.event(f"snapshot guardado: {path}", "good")

    def _do_ds2_scan(self, params: dict) -> None:
        """Probe DS2 modules -- needs the port, so the KWP71 session steps aside.

        DS2 uses even parity and no init, so it cannot share a session with the
        KWP71 DME. We close cleanly, scan, and let the main loop rebuild.
        """
        was_live = self._reader is not None
        self._teardown()
        self.publish(connected=False, live=None, status="buscando módulos DS2…")
        self.event("buscando módulos DS2 (EGS, ABS…)", "info")

        hits = []
        try:
            with DS2(self.port, timeout=1.0) as bus:
                for addr in DS2_ADDRESSES:
                    reply = bus.probe(addr)
                    if reply is None:
                        continue
                    text = reply.decode("ascii", "replace").strip()
                    hits.append({"address": f"0x{addr:02X}", "id": text,
                                 "raw": reply.hex(" ")})
                    self.event(f"módulo en 0x{addr:02X}: {text or reply.hex(' ')}", "good")
                    try:
                        faults = bus.read_faults(addr)
                        self.event(f"  fallas 0x{addr:02X}: {faults.hex(' ')}", "info")
                        hits[-1]["faults"] = faults.hex(" ")
                    except DS2Error as exc:
                        self.event(f"  sin memoria de fallas en 0x{addr:02X}: {exc}", "warn")
                    time.sleep(0.1)
        except Exception as exc:                          # noqa: BLE001
            self.event(f"escaneo DS2 falló: {exc}", "bad")

        if not hits:
            self.event("ningún módulo DS2 respondió", "warn")
        self.publish(ds2=hits)
        if not was_live:
            self.publish(status="modo sin conexión" if not self.enabled else "sin ECU")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- offline

    def _offline_faults(self) -> None:
        if self.state.get("faults"):
            return
        files = sorted(glob.glob("*.json")) + sorted(glob.glob("snapshots/*.json"))
        for path in reversed(files):
            try:
                with open(path) as fh:
                    data = json.load(fh)
                if "codes" in data:
                    self.publish(faults=data["codes"],
                                 faults_note=f"de {os.path.basename(path)}")
                    return
            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
                continue

    @staticmethod
    def _encode(codes) -> list[dict]:
        return [{
            "number": c.number, "description": c.description,
            "condition": c.condition, "conditions": c.conditions,
            "frequency": c.frequency, "rpm": c.rpm,
        } for c in codes]

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        self._do_record_stop({})


def make_handler(poller: Poller):
    ALLOWED = {"record_start", "record_stop", "refresh_faults", "snapshot", "ds2_scan"}

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args) -> None:
            pass

        def _send(self, body: bytes, ctype: str) -> None:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def _json(self, obj) -> None:
            self._send(json.dumps(obj).encode(), "application/json")

        def do_POST(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            if route.path != "/api/action":
                self.send_error(404)
                return
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            try:
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            except ValueError:
                self._json({"ok": False, "error": "json inválido"})
                return
            action = body.get("action", "")
            if action not in ALLOWED:
                self._json({"ok": False, "error": f"acción no permitida: {action}"})
                return
            poller.submit(action, body.get("params") or {})
            self._json({"ok": True, "queued": action})

        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            query = parse_qs(route.query)

            if route.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
                with open(STATIC, "rb") as fh:
                    self._send(fh.read(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")

            elif route.path == "/api/state":
                self._json(poller.snapshot_state())

            elif route.path == "/api/logs":
                self._json(sorted(glob.glob("*.csv"), reverse=True))

            elif route.path == "/api/log":
                name = (query.get("name") or [""])[0]
                # Only serve CSVs from the working directory -- no traversal.
                if not name or os.path.basename(name) != name or not name.endswith(".csv"):
                    self._json([])
                    return
                try:
                    with open(name, newline="") as fh:
                        self._json(list(csv.DictReader(fh)))
                except OSError:
                    self._json([])
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

    return Handler


def serve(port: str, http_port: int = 8036, address: int = 0x10,
          interval: float = 1.0, live: bool = True) -> None:
    poller = Poller(port, address, interval, enabled=live)
    poller.start()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", http_port), make_handler(poller))
    print(f"\n  Dashboard:  http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}")
    print(f"  ECU:        {'polling ' + port if live else 'desactivado (--no-live)'}")
    print("  Ctrl-C para salir\n")
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\ncerrando…")
    finally:
        poller.stop()
        server.server_close()

"""Local dashboard for the E36 DME.

Runs entirely on stdlib plus pyserial -- no framework, no CDN, nothing to
install. Everything is served from localhost.

The design constraint that shapes this: the K-line is a single serial port and
only one thing may own it. So exactly one background thread holds the ECU
session and publishes the latest sample into a shared dict; HTTP handlers only
ever read that dict. Browser requests never touch the port.

It is also useful with no car attached -- captured CSV logs and saved fault
snapshots render fine offline, which is most of what you want when reviewing
a session afterwards.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

from .faults import decode as decode_faults
from .kline import KLineError
from .live import LiveReader
from .sensors import CORE_SENSORS

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STATIC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "static", "dashboard.html")


class Poller(threading.Thread):
    """Owns the ECU session and republishes the latest sample."""

    def __init__(self, port: str, address: int, interval: float, enabled: bool) -> None:
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.port = port
        self.address = address
        self.interval = interval
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.state: dict = {
            "connected": False,
            "status": "sin ECU" if enabled else "modo sin conexión",
            "live": None,
            "ecu_id": None,
            "faults": [],
            "faults_note": "",
        }
        self._stop = threading.Event()

    def publish(self, **kw) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.state.update(kw)

    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return dict(self.state)

    def run(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            self._offline_faults()
            return
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                self._session()
            except (KLineError, OSError) as exc:
                log.debug("session failed: %s", exc)
                self.publish(connected=False, live=None,
                             status=f"sin ECU ({type(exc).__name__})")
                self._offline_faults()
                self._stop.wait(6.0)

    def _session(self) -> None:
        reader = LiveReader(self.port, address=self.address)
        with reader:
            session = reader._session
            ids = [s.decode("ascii", "replace").strip() for s in session.id_strings]
            self.publish(connected=True, status="conectada", ecu_id=ids)

            # Read fault memory once per session rather than every tick -- it
            # changes rarely and each read costs a full round trip.
            try:
                raw = b"".join(session.read_fault_codes())
                self.publish(faults=self._encode(decode_faults(raw)),
                             faults_note="leído de la ECU")
            except KLineError as exc:
                log.debug("fault read failed: %s", exc)

            while not self._stop.is_set():
                sample = reader.sample()
                if sample is None:
                    raise KLineError("perdimos la ECU")
                values = {s.name: round(s.scale(sample[s.name]), 3)
                          for s in CORE_SENSORS}
                self.publish(connected=True, live=values, status="conectada")
                self._stop.wait(self.interval)

    def _offline_faults(self) -> None:
        """With no ECU, fall back to the most recent saved snapshot."""
        if self.state.get("faults"):
            return
        files = sorted(glob.glob("*.json")) + sorted(glob.glob("snapshots/*.json"))
        for path in reversed(files):
            try:
                with open(path) as fh:
                    data = json.load(fh)
                if "codes" in data:
                    self.publish(faults=data["codes"],
                                 faults_note=f"de {os.path.basename(path)}")
                    return
            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
                continue

    @staticmethod
    def _encode(codes) -> list[dict]:
        return [{
            "number": c.number, "description": c.description,
            "condition": c.condition, "conditions": c.conditions,
            "frequency": c.frequency, "rpm": c.rpm,
        } for c in codes]

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()


def make_handler(poller: Poller):
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args) -> None:  # keep the console clean
            pass

        def _send(self, body: bytes, ctype: str) -> None:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def _json(self, obj) -> None:
            self._send(json.dumps(obj).encode(), "application/json")

        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            route = urlparse(self.path)
            query = parse_qs(route.query)

            if route.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
                with open(STATIC, "rb") as fh:
                    self._send(fh.read(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")

            elif route.path == "/api/state":
                self._json(poller.snapshot())

            elif route.path == "/api/logs":
                self._json(sorted(glob.glob("*.csv"), reverse=True))

            elif route.path == "/api/log":
                name = (query.get("name") or [""])[0]
                # Only serve CSVs from the working directory -- no traversal.
                if not name or os.path.basename(name) != name or not name.endswith(".csv"):
                    self._json([])
                    return
                try:
                    with open(name, newline="") as fh:
                        self._json(list(csv.DictReader(fh)))
                except OSError:
                    self._json([])
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

    return Handler


def serve(port: str, http_port: int = 8036, address: int = 0x10,
          interval: float = 1.0, live: bool = True) -> None:
    poller = Poller(port, address, interval, enabled=live)
    poller.start()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", http_port), make_handler(poller))
    print(f"\n  Dashboard:  http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}")
    print(f"  ECU:        {'polling ' + port if live else 'desactivado (--no-live)'}")
    print("  Ctrl-C para salir\n")
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\ncerrando…")
    finally:
        poller.stop()
        server.server_close()

**Acciones desde la UI**, todas encoladas al mismo hilo que tiene el puerto serie — nunca hay dos cosas peleándose por el device:

| Botón | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| **● Grabar** | Empieza a escribir CSV con las muestras en vivo; el botón muestra el contador y se convierte en ■ Detener |
| **Releer fallas** | Vuelve a leer la memoria del DME sin cortar la sesión |
| **Guardar snapshot** | Guarda la lectura actual en `snapshots/` con fecha — es la mitad del método antes/después |
| **Buscar EGS / módulos DS2** | Baja la sesión KWP71, escanea DS2, y deja que la sesión se reconstruya sola |

**La sección EGS ya está en la UI**, y es honesta sobre lo que no sabemos: mientras no se haya buscado explica por qué nunca apareció (habla DS2, no KWP71), y si el escaneo no encuentra nada lo dice sin inventar. Si algún módulo responde, muestra dirección, string de ID y la memoria de fallas **en hexadecimal crudo** — porque el formato de los códigos del EGS todavía no está decodificado, y poner una decodificación inventada ahí sería peor que mostrar hex.

Cuando consigamos una lectura real del EGS, con esos bytes más la tabla numerada que ya está en `docs/EGS_NOTES.md` se puede escribir el decodificador, igual que hicimos con el del DME.

Los botones se deshabilitan solos según el estado: grabar y releer fallas necesitan sesión viva, el escaneo DS2 funciona igual sin ECU porque de todas formas tira la sesión abajo.

Probado sin auto: acción no permitida rechazada, escaneo DS2 sin cable falla limpio y lo reporta en el log de eventos en vez de tumbar el servidor.

content.text:
Corriendo en **http://127.0.0.1:8036**

Lo que tomé de las fotos:

- **Ámbar sobre negro cálido**, con un degradado radial suave arriba que imita la luz cayendo sobre el tablero
- **Todo monoespaciado en mayúsculas con tracking abierto** — los títulos de sección leen como las etiquetas serigrafiadas del OBC (`CONSUM`, `RANGE`, `LIMIT`)
- **Bloom en lo encendido**: `text-shadow` en los números grandes y `drop-shadow` en las líneas de los gráficos, que es lo que hace que se vea retroiluminado y no simplemente naranja
- **Los botones imitan la botonera del OBC** — cajas con bisel, texto ámbar, y se encienden al pasar el mouse
- **Tiles como los segmentos del display**, número grande con glow y unidad apagada al lado

**Sobre el color, una decisión que vale explicar:** el ámbar exacto de BMW (~`#ff7a1a`) **no pasa** la validación — su luminosidad OKLCH cae en 0.72 y la banda para fondo oscuro es 0.48–0.67. Probé seis candidatos y el más brillante que pasa todos los checks es **`#d96f14`**, que es el que usan las líneas de los gráficos. El texto sí usa un ámbar más brillante (`#ffb37a`) porque el texto se juzga por contraste WCAG, que es otro criterio y lo pasa holgado.

Los colores de estado quedaron sin tocar — verde/ámbar/rojo son fijos por norma y además son exactamente los del tablero real. Siguen llevando ícono y etiqueta escrita, así que el color nunca es la única señal.

Es un diseño comprometido con un solo modo: un tablero es oscuro por naturaleza, así que saqué el modo claro en vez de dejarlo a medias.

content.text:
Recargá **http://127.0.0.1:8036** (Cmd+Shift+R para saltear caché).

**El tooltip: la causa era de scoping, no de estilo.** El `<div class="tip">` está fuera de `.viz-root`, y yo tenía las variables CSS declaradas *sobre* `.viz-root`. Un elemento fuera de ese subárbol no ve esas variables, así que `background: var(--surface-2)` quedaba sin valor — fondo transparente — y `color: var(--text-primary)` también, cayendo al negro por defecto del navegador. Exactamente lo que describiste.

Lo arreglé por dos vías independientes, para que no vuelva a pasar:

1. **Los tokens ahora viven en `:root`**, así cualquier elemento los ve esté donde esté en el árbol
2. **`.tip` declara además sus colores literales como fallback** (`background: #140d08; background: var(--surface-2, #140d08)`), así que aunque alguien vuelva a mover el scope, el tooltip sigue siendo legible

**Los íconos** son Lucide (MIT), descargados y embebidos inline — la página sigue sin depender de internet. Al ser stroke-based con `currentColor`, el octágono se pinta rojo, el triángulo ámbar y los del log verde/rojo/apagado según el evento, cosa que los emoji no permitían porque traían color propio.

Sobre SF Symbols: no existe como webfont y referenciar sus glifos por codepoint del sistema da tofu en cuanto cambia la versión, por eso fui a un pack real como pediste. Lucide es el más cercano en espíritu — mismo trazo fino y geometría de esquinas redondeadas.

Los `·` que quedan en el texto son separadores tipográficos (`ocurrencias 50 · registrada a 1880 rpm`), no íconos.

Confirmame si el tooltip ya se ve al pasar el mouse sobre un gráfico.

questions.question: ¿Hasta dónde puede llegar el dashboard en cuanto a acciones que ESCRIBEN en la ECU?

options.label: Lectura + borrar códigos (Recomendado)
options.description: Todo lo de lectura, más borrar la memoria de fallas con confirmación explícita. Sin nada que mueva actuadores. Es el equilibrio razonable: útil, y lo peor que puede pasar es perder evidencia.

options.label: Agregar tests de actuadores
options.description: Suma el bloque ACTIVATE_ACTUATOR (0x04): comandar la válvula del canister, la bomba de nafta, el actuador de ralentí, etc. Diagnosticaría el código 36 directamente (mandás la válvula y escuchás si clickea). Pero acciona hardware real con el motor ahí — y hay una fuga de nafta sin resolver.

options.label: Solo lectura, nada de escritura
options.description: Ni borrar códigos ni actuadores. El dashboard no puede modificar absolutamente nada en el auto. Máxima seguridad, cero riesgo de romper algo mientras no estás.

options.label: Todo, incluido escribir RAM/EEPROM
options.description: Suma WRITE_RAM y WRITE_EEPROM. Permitiría experimentar con adaptaciones, pero escribir mal en la EEPROM del DME puede dejarlo inutilizable. Solo si querés explícitamente esa capacidad.

questions.question: ¿Para qué querés que esté optimizado principalmente?

options.label: Investigar la caja + TPS (Recomendado)
options.description: Todo orientado a cerrar el diagnóstico: línea de tiempo de eventos, comparación de snapshots antes/después, captura desde arranque en frío, correlación entre canales, detección automática de anomalías. Herramienta de investigación.

options.label: Scanner general del auto
options.description: Equilibrado: leer todo lo que el DME expone, explorar direcciones de RAM, buscar canales desconocidos, mapear el ECU. Más de exploración y descubrimiento que de un problema puntual.

options.label: Tablero de a bordo en vivo
options.description: Enfocado en verlo mientras el auto anda: instrumentos grandes tipo cluster, agujas, alertas visuales, poca lectura y mucho vistazo. Menos análisis, más monitoreo en tiempo real.

options.label: Las tres cosas, con pestañas
options.description: Un dashboard con secciones separadas para cada uso. Más completo pero más superficie que puede fallar y más difícil de verificar sin el auto.

questions.question: ¿Lo abro solo en esta máquina o accesible desde el celular?

options.label: Solo localhost (Recomendado)
options.description: Como está ahora: 127.0.0.1, nadie más lo ve. Si querés mirarlo desde el celular después, se cambia con un flag.

options.label: Accesible en la red local
options.description: Bind a 0.0.0.0 para verlo desde el celular mientras la laptop está conectada en el vano motor, o mientras otro maneja. Muy útil en la práctica. Ojo: no tiene autenticación, así que cualquiera en tu red lo ve y puede tocar los botones.

options.label: Red local, pero con token
options.description: Accesible desde el celular, protegido con un token en la URL que se genera al arrancar. Más seguro que abrirlo sin más, y sigue siendo cómodo.

options.label: SQLite con historial completo (Recomendado)
options.description: Base local con todas las sesiones, muestras y snapshots. Permite comparar el ralentí de hoy contra el de la semana pasada, ver la evolución del contador de ocurrencias, y buscar cuándo apareció cada falla. Los CSV se siguen exportando igual.

options.label: Seguir con archivos sueltos
options.description: CSV y JSON como ahora. Simple, todo legible con cualquier herramienta, cero dependencias nuevas. Pero no hay comparación histórica ni tendencias más allá de abrir archivos a mano.

options.label: SQLite, pero solo resúmenes
options.description: Guarda métricas agregadas por sesión (ralentí medio, temperatura máxima, códigos presentes) en vez de cada muestra. Base chica y rápida; se pierde el detalle fino.

It currently shows: 5 live sensors (rpm, coolant temp, intake air temp, battery volts, injection load), decoded fault codes with freeze-frame data, CSV capture logs with line charts, and a DS2 module probe. Roughly 1 Hz sampling, round-trip bound.

Study these and anything else relevant, and report what is genuinely worth stealing:
- RealDash, Torque Pro, Car Scanner ELM OBD2 (commercial, for UX patterns)
- github.com/brendan-w/python-OBD, github.com/Ircama/ELM327-emulator
- FreeEMS / Speeduino / rusEFI TunerStudio dashboards (these are the serious ones — gauge layouts, log analysis)
- github.com/uholeschak/ediabaslib (BMW-specific, has an Android app "Deep OBD")
- Any open-source instrument-cluster or CAN dashboard projects
- Grafana/Prometheus automotive dashboards if any are illustrative

Answer concretely:
1. What FEATURES do serious diagnostic dashboards have that a naive one lacks? Be specific and prioritised — I want a ranked list, not a catalogue. Think: what does a mechanic or tuner actually reach for?
2. How do they present LOG ANALYSIS — replay/scrubbing through a recorded session, cursor-linked charts, marking events, comparing two runs overlaid?
3. What does a good ECU RAM/memory EXPLORER look like for reverse-engineering unknown addresses? (I know 5 addresses out of a 252-byte space and want to find more — e.g. TPS and road speed, which are still unlocated.)
4. Which derived/computed values are worth showing that aren't raw sensor reads? (e.g. estimated gear from rpm÷speed, load percentage, warm-up rate, idle stability metrics, injector duty cycle.)
5. What alerting/threshold patterns are standard — how do they warn without crying wolf?
6. Anything specific to intermittent-fault hunting: how do these tools help you catch a fault that happens for 200 ms once every twenty minutes?
7. Common UX mistakes these projects make that I should avoid.

End with a ranked "top 12 features to build, highest value first", each with a one-line justification and a rough complexity note (trivial / moderate / hard). Be opinionated and concrete. Prefer things implementable in vanilla JS with no dependencies.

input.description: Research instrument gauge design
input.prompt:
Research how to design and implement SERIOUS-looking automotive instrument gauges, and write a practical implementation guide to /Users/ignaciopardo/Desktop/E36_OBD/docs/GAUGE_DESIGN.md. Include actual reusable SVG/JS snippets in the document — this is a build guide another agent will follow.

Context: a local dark-themed web dashboard for a BMW E36, styled after the car's own amber/red-orange backlit instrument cluster on true black. Vanilla JS, inline SVG, no libraries, no CDN, must work offline. The palette is fixed: background #000000, panel #0d0906, series/needle #e0521a, lit text #ff8551, secondary #cf6a3c, muted #8a4526, borders #2b1a10. Monospace typography throughout.

Cover, concretely and with code:

1. **Analog gauge geometry.** How to lay out a circular gauge in SVG: sweep angle conventions (BMW tachometers typically sweep ~270°, starting lower-left), major/minor tick generation, numeral placement, the needle with a proper pivot hub. Give me a parameterised function `gauge({min,max,value,majorStep,minorStep,startAngle,sweep,...})` that returns SVG. Include the trig — I want the actual formulas, not prose.

2. **Redline / warning zones** as arc segments, and how to render them so they read at a glance without shouting.

3. **Needle animation.** Smooth movement between 1 Hz samples without lying about the data — critical-damped easing vs linear interpolation, and why a gauge that overshoots is misleading on a diagnostic tool. Give the actual easing approach.

4. **Linear/bar gauges** for temperature and fuel — how the real E36 does it (a segmented arc), and how to draw one.

5. **Warning lamp row** — how real clusters group and prioritise telltales, standard ISO symbols, and how to render them as inline SVG in lit/unlit states.

6. **Typography for instruments.** Numeral treatment, tabular figures, unit placement, label hierarchy, letter-spacing. What makes a readout look like an instrument rather than a web page.

7. **The "serious" quality bar.** What visually separates a professional instrument panel (think Bosch/VDO/Stack/AiM dashes, or TunerStudio) from a hobby project? Be specific about alignment grids, density, restraint, bezel/inset treatment, and where glow/bloom helps versus where it looks cheap.

8. **Digital readout blocks** — 7-segment style rendering in SVG or CSS, and when a digital readout beats an analog gauge (spoiler: precision vs rate-of-change; say which of my channels want which).

My channels: engine rpm (0-7000, redline ~6000), coolant temp (-30 to 130 °C, warn above 110), intake air temp (-30 to 80 °C), battery volts (8-16 V, warn below 13 or above 15 with engine running), injection load in ms (0-20).

Prioritise things I can implement in a few hundred lines of vanilla JS. Real, working code snippets over theory. Where you give a snippet, make sure the maths is correct — I will be pasting it in.
