# TOPIC A — Priority, ordering and grouping of telltales

## A1. The headline answer: no standard dictates physical ordering or grouping

**Well-sourced.** I read the complete text of FMVSS 101 and ECE R121 and searched both for any provision governing relative position, rows, left/right, or severity ordering. **There is none.** Every location requirement is of the form "must be visible to the driver" or "the identifier must be adjacent to the thing it identifies." Nothing constrains where a telltale sits relative to another telltale.

The only regulatory provisions that touch on *relationships between* telltales are the **common-space (shared-pixel) rules**, and those govern shared display real estate, not physical layout.

## A2. FMVSS 101 (49 CFR 571.101) — verbatim

Source: [govinfo CFR-2024-title49-vol6-sec571-101](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title49-vol6/xml/CFR-2024-title49-vol6-sec571-101.xml) · [Cornell LII mirror](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/571.101)

**Scope (S1):**
> "This standard specifies performance requirements for location, identification, color, and illumination of motor vehicle controls, telltales and indicators."

**Definition (S4):**
> "*Telltale* means an optical signal that, when illuminated, indicates the actuation of a device, a correct or improper functioning or condition, or a failure to function."

**Location — S5.1:**
> **S5.1.2** "The telltales and indicators listed in Table 1 and Table 2 and their identification must be located so that, when activated, they are visible to a driver under the conditions of S5.6.1 and S5.6.2."
>
> **S5.1.3** "Except as provided in S5.1.4, the identification for controls, telltales and indicators must be placed on or adjacent to the telltale, indicator or control that it identifies."

**The "conditions" — S5.6 (this is the answer to your driver's-seated-position question):**
> **S5.6.1** "The driver has adapted to the ambient light roadway conditions."
> **S5.6.2** "The driver is restrained by the seat belts installed in accordance with 49 CFR 571.208 and adjusted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's instructions."

**Important nuance:** FMVSS 101 does **not** use the phrase "normal seated position," and it does **not** invoke an eye-ellipse. The only stated conditions are light adaptation and being belted. The belted condition (S5.6.2) is the functional equivalent — it pins the driver into the seat so visibility is judged from a realistic head position, but the standard never defines an eye point.

Two *other* standards are stricter about seated-position visibility, and these are the ones worth quoting in a build guide:
- **FMVSS 105 S5.3**: brake indicator lamps must be "mounted in front of and in clear view of the driver."
- **FMVSS 208 S4.5.2**: the airbag readiness indicator "shall be clearly visible from the driver's designated seating position."
- **FMVSS 208 S19.2.2(d)** is the single most prescriptive placement rule in US law — and it applies only to the PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF telltale: it must be "located within the interior of the vehicle and forward of and above the design H-point of both the driver's and any front outboard passenger's seat in their forwardmost seating positions."

**Illumination — S5.3.1(e)** (critical for Topic B):
> "A telltale must not emit light except when identifying the malfunction or vehicle condition it is designed to indicate, or during a bulb check."

**Colour — S5.4:**
> **S5.4.1** "The light of each telltale listed in Table 1 must be of the color specified for that telltale in column 6 of that table."
> **S5.4.2** "Any indicator or telltale not listed in Table 1 … must not be a color that masks the driver's ability to recognize any telltale, control, or indicator listed in Table 1."

**Common space — S5.5. This is the only genuine priority scheme in US regulation:**
> **S5.5.2** "The telltales for any brake system malfunction required by Table 1 to be red, air bag malfunction, low tire pressure, electronic stability control malfunction …, passenger air bag off, high beam, turn signal, and seat belt **must not be shown in the same common space**."
>
> **S5.5.4** "…when the underlying conditions exist for actuation of two or more telltales, the messages must be either: (a) Repeated automatically in sequence, or (b) Indicated by visible means and capable of being selected for viewing by the driver…"
>
> **S5.5.5** "In the case of the telltale for a brake system malfunction, air bag malfunction, side air bag malfunction, low tire pressure, electronic stability control malfunction …, passenger air bag off, high beam, turn signal, or seat belt that is designed to display in a common space, that telltale **must displace any other symbol or message in that common space** while the underlying condition for the telltale's activation exists."
>
> **S5.5.6(b)** "Telltales for high beams, turn signal, low tire pressure, and passenger air bag off, and telltales for which the color red is required in Table 1 **must not be cancelable** while the underlying condition for their activation exists."

So: FMVSS **does** define a displacement priority and a non-cancellability rule — but only for pixels shared in a common space, and only as a two-tier scheme (the listed set beats everything else). There is no ranking *within* the privileged set, and no physical layout rule.

## A3. ECE R121 — governs location *and* identification *and* colour *and* illumination

Source: [EUR-Lex CELEX 42016X0108(01)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:42016X0108(01))

**Be precise here — your question assumed R121 might be symbol+colour only. It isn't.** Its formal title is "…the location and identification of hand controls, tell-tales and indicators," and paragraph 5 states:

> "A vehicle fitted with a control, a tell-tale or an indicator, listed in the Table, shall meet the prescribed requirements of this Regulation for the **location, identification and colour, and illumination** of such control, tell-tale or indicator."

**Scope (§1):**
> "This Regulation applies to vehicles of categories M and N. It specifies requirements for the location, identification, colour and illumination of motor vehicle hand controls, tell-tales and indicators. It is designed to ensure the accessibility and visibility of vehicle controls, tell-tales and indicators, and to facilitate their selection under daylight and night-time conditions, in order to reduce the safety hazards caused by the diversion of the driver's attention from the driving task and by mistakes in selecting controls."

**But "location" means only visibility + adjacency:**
> **5.1.2** "The tell-tales and indicators, shall be located so that they are visible and recognisable to a driver during night and day under the conditions of paragraphs 5.6.1 and 5.6.2. Tell-tales and indicators need not be visible or recognisable when not activated."
>
> **5.1.3** "The identifications of tell-tales, indicators and controls shall be placed on or adjacent to the tell-tales, indicators and controls that they identify…"

**The one hard placement rule (5.1.4)** — again, only for passenger airbag off:
> "Notwithstanding paragraphs 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.1.3 the tell-tale for 'passenger air bag off', if fitted, must be located within the interior of the vehicle and forward of and above the design H-point of both the driver's and the front passenger(s)' seat in their forward most seating positions."

**R121 common-space priority (5.5.1) — mirrors FMVSS but with a narrower privileged set:**
> **5.5.1.3** "The tell-tales for the brake system malfunction, headlamp driving beam, direction indicator and seat belt shall not be shown in the same common space,"
> **5.5.1.4** "If tell-tale for the brake system malfunction, headlamp driving beam, direction indicator or seat belt is displayed in a common space it must displace any other symbol in such common space if the underlying condition exists for its activation,"
> **5.5.1.5** "With the exception of tell-tales for the brake system malfunction, headlamp driving beam, direction indicator or seat belt, the information may be cancellable automatically or by the driver,"
> **5.5.1.6** "Unless prescribed in a specific Regulation, the colour requirements regarding tell-tales do not apply when tell-tales appear in a common space."

That last one (5.5.1.6) is a genuinely surprising provision worth flagging in a build guide: **in a shared digital display, ECE colour requirements lapse.**

R121 also defers colour semantics to ISO: **5.4.2** says colour choice "shall follow the guidelines specified in paragraph 5 of standard ISO 2575:2004," and **5.4.1.1** allows re-colouring of certain footnoted symbols "according to the general colour coding as proposed in paragraph 5 of standard ISO 2575:2004."

**Approval paperwork (3.2.4)** requires "Drawings and/or photographs showing the layout of controls and location of tell-tales and indicators in the vehicle" — so layout is *documented and approved*, but not *prescribed*.

## A4. ISO standards — what each one actually is

| Standard | Actual title | What it does | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ISO 2575:2021** (+A1:2024) | Road vehicles — Symbols for controls, indicators and tell-tales | Symbol library + colour-coding guidance (§5). **No layout.** | Title/year sourced; §5 content inferred from R121's cross-references |
| **ISO 4040:2009** | Road vehicles — Location of hand controls, indicators and tell-tales in motor vehicles | Applies to "hand-operated controls, to indicators and to tell-tales in all motor vehicles, excluding motorcycles and mopeds." Specifies location by "subdividing the space within reach of drivers into specific **zones**, to which certain controls essential to the safe operation of vehicles are assigned." | Scope from reseller abstract — **paywalled, I could not read the standard text** |
| **ISO 15008:2017** | Road vehicles — Ergonomic aspects of TICS — Specifications and test procedures for **in-vehicle visual presentation** | Legibility: character height, contrast, luminance. **Not** a priority scheme. | Title/year sourced |
| **ISO/TS 16951:2021** | Road vehicles — Ergonomic aspects of TICS — **Procedures for determining priority of on-board messages presented to drivers** | ← **This is the standard you were reaching for.** | Title/year sourced; procedure content paywalled |

**Critical correction on ISO 4040:** its zone system is for *hand controls* (reach envelopes). For indicators and tell-tales it addresses *visibility*, not zoning. So even the one ISO standard with "location of… tell-tales" in its title does not give you a tell-tale grid. Flagging this as **moderate confidence** — the abstract is clear that zones are assigned to "controls," but I could not read the body text to rule out a tell-tale zone annex.

## A5. SAE — two corrections to your premises

- **SAE J2402** — "Road Vehicles — Symbols for Controls, Indicators and Tell-Tales." Symbols only, harmonized with ISO 2575. **No location, grouping or ordering content.** (Stabilized Nov 2023.)
- **SAE J1053** — **this is not a telltale standard.** A standards listing gives its title as "Steel Stamped Nuts of One Pitch Thread Design — Inch Series." *Moderate confidence* — single source, but the scope text quoted is clearly fastener content. I'd drop J1053 from the guide unless you can verify otherwise.
- The SAE documents that OEMs actually use for telltale *visibility* are **SAE J941 "Motor Vehicle Drivers' Eye Locations"** (the eyellipse) and **SAE J1050 "Describing and Measuring the Driver's Field of View."** These determine whether a proposed telltale position is legal under FMVSS 101 S5.1.2 / R121 5.1.2. *Titles confirmed; their application to telltale placement is my inference, not a sourced claim.*

## A6. The "red central / amber peripheral" convention — NOT documented

**This is the weakest claim in your outline and I want to be blunt about it.** I searched for OEM style guides, published research, and engineering sources on grouping red critical lamps near the driver's line of sight with amber to the periphery. **I found no authoritative source.** Consumer-facing sources discuss *colour-coded urgency* (red = stop now, amber = service soon) but not *spatial placement*.

Two things I can offer instead:

1. **A real OEM data point**, from BMW factory service data for the E36 ([charm.li](https://charm.li/BMW/1995/325i%20%28E36%29%20L6-2494cc%202.5L%20DOHC%20%28M50%20TU%29/Repair%20and%20Diagnosis/Instrument%20Panel%2C%20Gauges%20and%20Warning%20Indicators/Description%20and%20Operation/Instrument%20Cluster%20Display%20Functions/)):
   > "**Indicator and Warning Lamps** — The various lamps are positioned at the top center and along the bottom of the cluster display. They are controlled internally by the cluster or externally by other sensors and modules **where required by legislation**."

   Note what that says: top-centre and bottom rows, and the split between cluster-driven and externally-driven lamps is legislation-driven. It does *not* say red-vs-amber drove the placement.

2. **The honest framing for your guide:** the convention is real as an observed pattern but is emergent, not codified. It falls out of (a) colour semantics from ISO 2575 / Table 1 of FMVSS 101, (b) the eyellipse/field-of-view constraint that anything safety-critical must be inside the steering-wheel aperture, and (c) the common-space displacement rules. Present it as a design heuristic, not a requirement.

**One caveat on my search coverage:** I could not retrieve NHTSA's *Human Factors Design Guidance for Driver-Vehicle Interfaces* (DOT HS 812 360, Dec 2016) — nhtsa.gov and rosap.ntl.bts.gov both returned 403 to automated fetches. That document is the most likely place to find published guidance on telltale prioritization and location, and it is **an outstanding gap**. Worth a manual download.

## A7. Modern digital clusters — documented priority schemes

Three layers, in descending order of legal force:

1. **Regulatory (binding):** FMVSS 101 S5.5.2–S5.5.6 and ECE R121 5.5.1.1–5.5.1.6, quoted above. Displacement + non-cancellability + no-co-location for a privileged set.
2. **Standardized method (voluntary):** ISO/TS 16951:2021, procedures for determining message priority.
3. **OEM-specific.** A nice period example from the E36's own Check Control ([charm.li](https://charm.li/BMW/1995/325i%20%28E36%29%20L6-2494cc%202.5L%20DOHC%20%28M50%20TU%29/Repair%20and%20Diagnosis/Accessories%20and%20Optional%20Equipment/Trip%20Computer/Description%20and%20Operation/Driver%20Information%20Systems/Check%20Control/)) — a real three-tier scheme shipping in 1992:
   > "**PRIORITY 1:** The brake light circuit is the only priority 1 fault display… The warning triangles in the display will flash and the check warning lamp in the cluster will also flash for 20 seconds, then remain on steady. Pressing the check button on the matrix panel will cancel the display for 5 seconds and then it will reappear…
   > **PRIORITY 2:** These failures will appear in the display as soon as they occur… Priority 2 failures are only posted for 20 seconds and then are canceled…
   > **PRIORITY 3:** Low Coolant Level is the only priority three display. This condition will not be displayed while driving."

---

# TOPIC B — Bulb check / self-test on ignition-on

## B1. Yes, the bulb check IS legally mandated — but not where you thought

**Your premise was half right.** The mandate lives in the *individual system* standards, not in the telltale standards. FMVSS 101 and ECE R121 only *permit* a bulb check; they never require one.

### US — mandatory lamp checks (all well-sourced, verbatim)

**FMVSS 105 S5.3.2 (hydraulic/electric brake systems)** — [govinfo](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title49-vol6/xml/CFR-2024-title49-vol6-sec571-105.xml):
> "(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, **all indicator lamps shall be activated as a check of lamp function** either when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the 'on' (run) position when the engine is not running, or when the ignition (start) switch is in a position between 'on' (run) and 'start' that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position.
> (b) The indicator lamps need not be activated when a starter interlock is in operation."

FMVSS 105 S5.3.3(b) adds the extinguish rule for heavy vehicles:
> "The indicator lamp shall be deactivated at the end of the check of lamp function unless there is a malfunction or a message about a malfunction that existed when the key switch was last turned to the 'off' position."

**FMVSS 135 S5.5.2 (light vehicle brake systems)** — note this one uniquely allows a *manual* check:
> "**Function check.** (a) All indicators shall be activated as a check function by either: (1) Automatic activation when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the 'on' ('run') position when the engine is not running, or when the ignition ('start') switch is in a position between 'on' ('run') and 'start' that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position, or (2) A single manual action by the driver, such as momentary activation of a test button or switch mounted on the instrument panel in front of and in clear view of the driver…
> (c) The manufacturer shall explain the brake check function test procedure in the owner's manual."

**FMVSS 126 S5.3.4 (ESC malfunction telltale)**:
> "…each ESC malfunction telltale must be activated as a check of lamp function either when the ignition locking system is turned to the 'On' ('Run') position when the engine is not running, or when the ignition locking system is in a position between 'On' ('Run') and 'Start' that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position."

with **S5.3.6** "The requirement S5.3.4 does not apply to telltales shown in a common space," and a dedicated test procedure headed "**Telltale bulb check.**"

**FMVSS 138 S4.3.3(a) (low tire pressure telltale)** — same construction, plus S4.4(b)(4)(i) for the dedicated TPMS malfunction telltale.

### UNECE — mandatory brake/ABS self-check

**UN R13-H para 5.2.21.4** ([EUR-Lex CELEX 42023X0401](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:42023X0401)) — this is the exact clause you were after:
> "The warning signal(s) mentioned above **shall light up when the electrical equipment of the vehicle (and the braking system) is energised. With the vehicle stationary, the braking system shall verify that none of the specified failures or defects are present before extinguishing the signals.** Specified failures or defects which should activate the warning signals mentioned above, but which are not detected under static conditions, shall be stored upon detection and be displayed at start-up and at all times when the ignition (start) switch is in the 'On' (run) position, as long as the failure or defect persists."

**UN R13 para 5.2.1.29.5** ([EUR-Lex CELEX 42016X0218(01)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:42016X0218(01))) is word-for-word identical. So both the passenger-car regulation (R13-H) and the general regulation (R13) mandate it.

Supporting context in R13-H:
> **5.2.21.1.1** "A **red** warning signal, indicating failures … which preclude achievement of the prescribed service braking performance and/or which preclude the functioning of at least one of two independent service braking circuits;"
> **5.2.21.1.2** "Where applicable, a **yellow** warning signal indicating an electrically detected defect within the vehicle braking equipment, which is not indicated by the red warning signal…"
> **5.2.21.3.3** "The warning signal shall be constant (not flashing)."

**ABS specifically — R13-H Annex 6, para 4.1:**
> "Any electrical failure or sensor anomaly that affects the system with respect to the functional and performance requirements in this annex, including those in the supply of electricity, the external wiring to the controller(s), the controller(s) and the modulator(s) shall be signalled to the driver by a specific optical warning signal. **The yellow warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.2. of this Regulation shall be used for this purpose.**"
> **4.1.1** "Sensor anomalies, which cannot be detected under static conditions, shall be detected not later than when the vehicle speed exceed 10 km/h. However, to prevent erroneous fault indication when a sensor is not generating a vehicle speed output, due to non-rotation of a wheel, verification may be delayed but detected not later than when the vehicle speed exceeds 15 km/h."

That 10/15 km/h clause is why an ABS lamp can extinguish at key-on and then re-illuminate once you're rolling — worth calling out in a build guide.

### The permissive clauses (US and EU)

- **FMVSS 101 S5.3.1(e):** "A telltale must not emit light except when identifying the malfunction or vehicle condition it is designed to indicate, **or during a bulb check**."
- **ECE R121 5.3.5:** "A tell-tale shall not emit light except when identifying the malfunction or vehicle condition for whose indication it is designed **or during a bulb check**."

Both are *exceptions to a prohibition*. They make a bulb check lawful; they do not require it, and neither specifies a duration.

## B2. FMVSS 208 airbag readiness — your premise is INCORRECT

**Well-sourced negative finding.** I pulled the complete text of 49 CFR 571.208 (354k characters) and searched it. **There is no mandated illuminate-then-extinguish sequence and no duration for the airbag readiness indicator.** S4.5.2 in its entirety:

> "**S4.5.2 Readiness indicator.** An occupant protection system that deploys in the event of a crash shall have a monitoring system with a readiness indicator. The indicator shall monitor its own readiness and shall be clearly visible from the driver's designated seating position. If the vehicle is equipped with a single readiness indicator for both a driver and passenger air bag, and if the vehicle is equipped with an on-off switch permitted by S4.5.4 of this standard, the readiness indicator shall monitor the readiness of the driver air bag when the passenger air bag has been deactivated by means of the on-off switch, and shall not illuminate solely because the passenger air bag has been deactivated by the manual on-off switch. A list of the elements of the system being monitored by the indicator shall be included with the information furnished in accordance with S4.5.1 but need not be included on the label."

That's all of it. "Shall monitor its own readiness" is the only self-test language, and it prescribes no behaviour.

Searches for "check of lamp function," "not less than N seconds," "bulb check," and "self-test" across the whole of 571.208 return **only**:

- **S19.2.2(h)** — and this is the PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF telltale, not the readiness lamp: "The telltale must not emit light except when any passenger air bag is turned off **or during a bulb check upon vehicle starting**." (Permissive again.)
- The seat belt warning timings, below.

**Where your "1 to 8 seconds" memory almost certainly comes from — FMVSS 208 S7.3, the SEAT BELT warning:**
> "S7.3 (a) A seat belt assembly provided at the driver's seating position shall be equipped with a warning system that, at the option of the manufacturer, either—
> (1) Activates a continuous or intermittent audible signal for a period of **not less than 4 seconds and not more than 8 seconds** and that activates a continuous or flashing warning light visible to the driver displaying the identifying symbol for the seat belt telltale shown in Table 2 of FMVSS 101 … **for not less than 60 seconds** (beginning when the vehicle ignition switch is moved to the 'on' or the 'start' position) when condition (b) exists simultaneously with condition (c), or that
> (2) Activates, **for a period of not less than 4 seconds and not more than 8 seconds** (beginning when the vehicle ignition switch is moved to the 'on' or the 'start' position), a continuous or flashing warning light visible to the driver … when condition (b) exists, and a continuous or intermittent audible signal when condition (b) exists simultaneously with condition (c)."

So the real number is **4 to 8 seconds**, it is the **seat belt** warning, and it is not a bulb check — it is a genuine unbelted-occupant warning. (S4.5.3.3(b) repeats 4–8 s audible / 60 s light for automatic belts.)

**ECE R94 / R121 airbag self-check — NOT VERIFIED.** R121's Table lists "Airbag malfunction" and "Side airbag malfunction" telltales (and specifies colour), but R121 prescribes no check sequence. I did not retrieve R94 itself. **Treat "ECE R94 mandates an airbag telltale self-check" as unverified — I would not put it in the guide without checking R94 directly.**

## B3. Durations in practice — no regulatory basis at all

**Important finding: not one of the regulations above specifies a bulb-check duration.** FMVSS 105/126/135/138 say "activated as a check of lamp function" and, at most, "deactivated at the end of the check." UN R13/R13-H say the signals extinguish once the system "shall verify that none of the specified failures or defects are present," which is a completion condition, not a clock.

The commonly repeated "2–4 seconds" figure is **industry practice, not regulation, and I could not find an authoritative source for it.** I'd recommend stating it as an observed norm and citing concrete measured examples instead. Two hard, sourced examples I did find, both BMW:

- **SRS lamp: 5 seconds** (E36, below).
- **Brake pad wear lamp: 30 seconds** (E36, below).

Neither matches "2–4 s," which should make you cautious about the claim.

## B4. Which lamps DON'T bulb-check, and why — the mechanism is regulatory

**Well-sourced, and this is the cleanest explanation available.** UN R48 ([EUR-Lex CELEX 42021X1718](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:42021X1718)) defines two fundamentally different telltale types:

> "**'Operating tell-tale'** means a visual or auditory signal (or any equivalent signal) indicating that a device has been switched ON and is operating correctly or not."
>
> "**'Closed-circuit tell-tale'** means a visual (or any equivalent signal) indicating that a device has been switched ON, but not indicating whether it is operating correctly or not."

And **5.13**: "Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by this Regulation it may be replaced by an 'operating' tell-tale."

R48 then assigns, per lamp:
- **6.1.8 Main-beam headlamp:** "Circuit-closed tell-tale mandatory."
- **6.3.8 Front fog lamp:** "Circuit-closed tell-tale mandatory. An independent non-flashing warning light."
- **6.6.8 Hazard warning signal:** "Flashing circuit-closed tell-tale mandatory."
- **6.9.8 Front position lamps:** "Circuit-closed tell-tale mandatory. This tell-tale shall be non-flashing and shall not be required if the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps."
- **6.11.8 Rear fog lamp:** "Circuit-closed tell-tale mandatory. An independent non-flashing warning light."

**That is the answer to "why don't high beams and fog lamps bulb-check":** a circuit-closed telltale is, by regulatory definition, a state indicator wired to the lamp circuit. It reports switch position. There is no fault state for it to self-test, and lighting it at key-on would actively violate FMVSS 101 S5.3.1(e) / R121 5.3.5 (which forbid a telltale emitting light except for its own condition or a bulb check).

**Turn signals are the interesting exception** — R48 6.5.8 requires an *operating* telltale:
> "Operating tell-tale mandatory for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b. It may be visual or auditory or both. If it is visual it shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of these direction-indicator lamps, is either extinguished, or remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency…"

So the turn signal telltale *does* have fault-reporting behaviour (the classic hyperflash) — but it is monitored *continuously while in use*, never at key-on. Note also FMVSS 101 S5.5.6(b) forbids high-beam and turn-signal telltales being cancelable.

## B5. BMW E36 specifics

Source throughout: BMW factory service data mirrored at [charm.li](https://charm.li/) (1995 325i E36 M50TU). This is licensed OEM/aftermarket service data — high quality, but a mirror, so treat as strong secondary.

### There is no automatic whole-cluster bulb check at key-on

**Well-sourced by absence + mechanism.** The E36 service data documents no automatic all-lamp sweep at ignition-on. Lamps illuminate individually according to their sensor/module state, and the cluster description explicitly says lamps are "controlled internally by the cluster **or externally by other sensors and modules** where required by legislation."

For a build guide, the important consequence: on an E36 several lamps light at key-on as a *physical side effect*, not as a designed self-test — e.g. the charge lamp lights because alternator field current flows through it, and the oil pressure lamp lights because the pressure switch is closed at zero pressure. **This mechanism reasoning is my inference from how these circuits work, not a quote from the E36 manual — flag it as such if you use it.**

### There IS a deliberate self-test, and it is on key position 1, not 2

From "Instrument Cluster Testing" ([link](https://charm.li/BMW/1995/325i%20%28E36%29%20L6-2494cc%202.5L%20DOHC%20%28M50%20TU%29/Repair%20and%20Diagnosis/Instrument%20Panel%2C%20Gauges%20and%20Warning%20Indicators/Description%20and%20Operation/Instrument%20Cluster%20Testing/)):

> "**1992 - 1996 E36 - 4 door/Coupe/Convertible/M3**
> … There is a self test that can be carried out on the cluster by **pressing the trip odometer reset button and switching the ignition to KL R**. All gauges move from the zero position to the maximum display and back again. **The warning lamps are illuminated as a bulb check.**
> In addition, vehicle specific data is displayed in the LCD matrix as follows: BMW PART NUMBER (6 digits), CODE NUMBER (5 digits), K NUMBER (4 digits), CHASSIS NUMBER (5 digits), SOFTWARE VERSION (3 digits), REVISION INDEX (2 digits).
> **The self test is canceled by switching the ignition off or to KL 15.**"

**Note the terminal designations carefully** — this is a detail that trips people up. The test is entered at **KL R (terminal R, key position 1)** and is *cancelled* by going to **KL 15 (ignition on, key position 2)**. So the E36 bulb check is explicitly *not* a position-2 behaviour.

For 1997–98 E36, E36/5 318ti and Z3, this became a 15-function test menu:
> "**TEST NO. 01: INSTRUMENT CLUSTER SELF TEST** - All of the gauges are activated and the warming lamps are illuminated as an output test as described on the previous page. At the end of the test, the cluster exits the test mode."

with entry described in "Check Function of Instrument Cluster" as: "Activation occurs with depressed reset button on trip-distance counter (TWSZ) when vehicle terminal R is selected at the same time."

### SRS lamp: 5 seconds — the one true timed self-test

From "BMW (SRS) Self Diagnostic System" ([link](https://charm.li/BMW/1995/325i%20%28E36%29%20L6-2494cc%202.5L%20DOHC%20%28M50%20TU%29/Repair%20and%20Diagnosis/Restraints%20and%20Safety%20Systems/Air%20Bag%20Systems/Testing%20and%20Inspection/Initial%20Inspection%20and%20Diagnostic%20Overview/BMW%20%28SRS%29%20Self%20Diagnostic%20System/)):

> "**Each time the ignition is switched 'On', the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) does a self-test. This is indicated by illumination of the SRS Warning Lamp for five seconds, after which the lamp extinguishes (standby mode) if no faults are detected.** Along with internal checks, the integrity of the following external circuits is checked:
> - All igniter circuits for shorts to ground or B+, and resistance range
> - **SRS Warning Lamp for open or shorts to ground or B+**
> - Safety Belt Buckle Contacts for open, shorted, and resistance range
> - Seat Occupancy Detector (SBE) message validity (when installed)"

Note the lamp itself is one of the monitored circuits. Fault responses are tiered:
> "'Minor' faults (such as seat buckle contact failure)… illuminate the SRS warning lamp for about **two minutes**, and then the lamp goes out. — 'Non-critical' faults (such as igniter resistance)… the warning lamp is illuminated continuously, but the system is still fully operational. — 'Critical' faults, such as accelerometer failure… The warning lamp is illuminated continuously, the Processor sets a fault and disables the system via the IGNITION TRIGGER SHUTDOWN."

The E36 SRS controller is the **ZAE** ("Central Airbag Trigger Module"), introduced for MY1994 across E31/E34/E36; system components explicitly include the "SRS warning lamp."

### Brake pad wear lamp: 30-second start-up illumination

From "Brake Warning Indicator: Testing and Inspection" ([link](https://charm.li/BMW/1995/325i%20%28E36%29%20L6-2494cc%202.5L%20DOHC%20%28M50%20TU%29/Repair%20and%20Diagnosis/Brakes%20and%20Traction%20Control/Brake%20Warning%20Indicator/Testing%20and%20Inspection/)):

> "The brake pad wear symbol illuminates when an open condition exists in the brake pad sensor circuit. **Once the circuit is rectified the brake pad wear indicator will shut off after first 30 seconds of switching the ignition on.**"
> "Condition: Brake Pad Wear indicator stays ON **after the 30 second start-up bulb check**."

The manual itself calls this a "bulb check" — a useful concrete counterexample to the "2–4 seconds" folklore.

### Check Control is optional equipment

> "The Check Control is an active warning system that displays various lighting circuit failures and low fluid level warnings. **It is only available on the listed models if they are equipped with the Multi-Function Clock or On-board Computer.** … The lighting circuits are **warm monitored only** - a fault will only be detected when the circuit is on."

Monitored: windshield washer fluid, low beam headlights, brake light circuit (incl. switch), coolant level, tail lights, license plate lights. Priorities 1/2/3 as quoted in A7. Low coolant (priority 3) "is also posted for 20 seconds when the ignition is switched on."

### E30 — not researched

I did not investigate the E30 cluster. Do not carry the E36 findings across; the E30 predates the ZAE and most E30s have no ABS-era self-test architecture.

---

# Summary: confidence ledger

**Well-sourced (verbatim regulation text retrieved and quoted):**
- No standard prescribes telltale ordering/grouping/rows — FMVSS 101 and ECE R121 read in full
- FMVSS 101 S5.1/S5.2/S5.3/S5.4/S5.5/S5.6 including the S5.5 common-space priority scheme
- ECE R121 governs location + identification + colour + illumination (not symbol/colour only)
- ECE R121 5.5.1.6 — colour requirements lapse in a common space
- Mandatory lamp checks: FMVSS 105 S5.3.2, 135 S5.5.2, 126 S5.3.4, 138 S4.3.3(a); UN R13-H 5.2.21.4, UN R13 5.2.1.29.5, R13-H Annex 6 §4.1/4.1.1
- **FMVSS 208 does NOT mandate an airbag bulb-check sequence or duration** (S4.5.2 quoted complete)
- The 4–8 s figure belongs to the seat belt warning (S7.3), not the airbag lamp
- No regulation anywhere specifies a bulb-check duration
- UN R48 circuit-closed vs operating telltale definitions and per-lamp assignments
- BMW E36: SRS 5 s self-test; 30 s brake-pad-wear start-up; self-test at KL R via trip reset; Check Control priorities 1/2/3

**Moderate confidence (secondary source or abstract only):**
- ISO 4040:2009 zone system applies to hand controls, not a telltale grid (abstract only — standard is paywalled)
- ISO 2575 / ISO 15008 / ISO/TS 16951 titles and scopes (reseller listings)
- SAE J2402 = symbols only; SAE J1053 is a fastener standard, not telltale-related (single source)

**Inferred / explicitly NOT sourced — do not present as fact:**
- "Red grouped centrally, amber peripheral" as a documented OEM convention — **no source found**
- SAE J941/J1050 being the tools used for telltale visibility compliance — plausible, my inference
- E36 charge/oil lamps lighting at key-on as a circuit side-effect rather than a designed test — my inference
- "2–4 seconds typical" — **no source found**; contradicted by the two BMW figures I did source

**Outstanding gaps worth chasing manually:**
- NHTSA DOT HS 812 360 *Human Factors Design Guidance for Driver-Vehicle Interfaces* — blocked (403) on both nhtsa.gov and rosap.ntl.bts.gov; most likely home of published telltale prioritization/location guidance
- ECE R94 — not retrieved; your claim about a mandated airbag self-check under R94 is unverified
- ISO 4040 and ISO/TS 16951 body text — paywalled</result>

---
name: e36-dashboard
description: The local web instrument panel for the E36 — how it is built, what it deliberately refuses to do, and how to run it
metadata:
  type: project
---

Local instrument panel for [[e36-obd1-kline-project]], at `~/Desktop/E36_OBD`, run with `./.venv/bin/python -m e36obd dash`. Python stdlib plus pyserial only — no framework, no CDN, works offline. Four hash-addressable tabs: `#tablero` (analog gauges), `#diagnostico` (faults, DS2/EGS probe, snapshot diff), `#capturas` (log analysis), `#scanner` (RAM explorer).

Flags: `--lan` binds 0.0.0.0 with a generated token (constant-time compare, also accepted as cookie or `X-Token`); `--demo` generates synthetic but physically plausible data so the panel can be developed and shown with no car; `--no-live` never opens the port.

**The architectural constraint:** the K-line is one serial port and only one thing may own it. Exactly ONE thread touches serial — it holds the live session and drains an action queue between samples. HTTP handlers never open the port; they enqueue and poll. That is why recording, fault reads, RAM dumps and DS2 probing coexist with live polling.

**Deliberate refusals, enforced server-side rather than hidden in the UI:** block titles `0x02` WriteRAM, `0x1A` WriteEEPROM and `0x04` ActivateActuator are rejected before reaching the bus (unit-tested with a fake ECU). Clearing fault memory IS allowed but always writes an automatic snapshot first, because the occurrence counters are the only evidence of how often a fault happens.

**Visual language:** red-orange on true black, monospace, deliberate single dark mode. Series colour `#e0521a` was chosen by running the palette validator, not by eye — BMW's actual amber (~`#ff7a1a`) fails the dark-mode lightness band at OKLCH L 0.72. Icons are Lucide (MIT) inlined so they take `currentColor`. The car blueprint is extracted from Ignacio's own `~/Desktop/Project-BMW-E36/Frame 465.pdf` via `pdftocairo`, filtered to drop dimension rules, rounded to 1 decimal.

**How to apply:** charts are one-per-channel on purpose — rpm/°C/V/ms differ by orders of magnitude and a shared axis would be a dual-axis chart. Every axis has a `minRange` floor so sensor quantization (0.068 V, 0.65 °C per count) does not render as a dramatic spike. Needles use a first-order lag that never overshoots, because a springy needle lies about the data between 1 Hz samples.

Exactly ONE thread touches serial — it holds the live session and drains an action queue between samples. HTTP handlers never open the port; they enqueue and poll. That is why recording, fault reads, RAM dumps and DS2 probing coexist with live polling.

**Deliberate refusals, enforced server-side rather than hidden in the UI:** block titles `0x02` WriteRAM, `0x1A` WriteEEPROM and `0x04` ActivateActuator are rejected before reaching the bus (unit-tested with a fake ECU). Clearing fault memory IS allowed but always writes an automatic snapshot first, because the occurrence counters are the only evidence of how often a fault happens.

**Visual language:** red-orange on true black, monospace, deliberate single dark mode. Series colour `#e0521a` was chosen by running the palette validator, not by eye — BMW's actual amber (~`#ff7a1a`) fails the dark-mode lightness band at OKLCH L 0.72. Icons are Lucide (MIT) inlined so they take `currentColor`. The car blueprint is extracted from Ignacio's own `~/Desktop/Project-BMW-E36/Frame 465.pdf` via `pdftocairo`, filtered to drop dimension rules, coordinates rounded to 1 decimal (3.1 MB → 148 KB).

**How to apply:** charts are one-per-channel on purpose — rpm/°C/V/ms differ by orders of magnitude and a shared axis would be a dual-axis chart. Every axis has a `minRange` floor so sensor quantization (0.068 V, 0.65 °C per count) does not render as a dramatic spike. Needles use a first-order lag that never overshoots, because a springy needle lies about the data between 1 Hz samples.

# ECU tuning / RAM-watch tool conventions: interaction models & definition schemas

**Bonus finding first, because it may short-circuit your whole project:** RomRaider ships a **BMW DS2 logger definition for MS41/MS42/MS43** with real RAM addresses. If your E36 is an M52 on MS41.1, TPS and road speed are already published. See §6.

---

## 1. RomRaider

### 1.1 The Logger definition DTD (verbatim, authoritative)

Source: `https://github.com/RomRaider/RomRaider/blob/master/definitions/logger.dtd`

```dtd
<!ELEMENT address ( #PCDATA ) >
<!ATTLIST address length CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST address bit ( 0 | 1 | ... | 31 ) #IMPLIED >

<!ELEMENT conversion ( replace* ) >
<!ATTLIST conversion expr        CDATA #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST conversion format      ( 0 | 0.0 | 0.00 | 0.000 | 0.0000 | 0.00000 | 0.000000) #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST conversion storagetype ( int8 | int16 | uint8 | uint16 | int32 | uint32 | float ) #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST conversion endian      CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST conversion units       CDATA #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST conversion gauge_min   CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST conversion gauge_max   CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST conversion gauge_step  CDATA #IMPLIED >

<!ELEMENT parameter ( ( address+, conversions?) | (depends, conversions?) ) >
<!ATTLIST parameter target CDATA #REQUIRED >      <!-- 1=ECU 2=TCU 3=both -->
<!ATTLIST parameter ecubit ( 0..7 ) #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST parameter ecubyteindex CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST parameter desc CDATA #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST parameter name CDATA #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST parameter id ID #REQUIRED >

<!ELEMENT ecuparam ( ecu+, conversions? ) >
<!ATTLIST ecuparam groupsize CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST ecuparam subgroup  CDATA #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST ecuparam group     CDATA #IMPLIED >
...
<!ELEMENT replace EMPTY >
<!ATTLIST replace value CDATA #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST replace with  CDATA #REQUIRED >

<!ELEMENT switch EMPTY >
<!ATTLIST switch bit ( 0..7 ) #REQUIRED >
<!ATTLIST switch byte CDATA #REQUIRED >
```

**Critical: one parameter can have N conversions.** The unit is not a label — it's a selector. The user picks °C vs °F vs raw at runtime and each carries its *own* expression, format, and gauge range. This is the single most important convention to steal.

### 1.2 Parser defaults (from `LoggerDefinitionHandler.java`)

`https://github.com/RomRaider/RomRaider/blob/master/src/main/java/com/romraider/logger/ecu/definition/xml/LoggerDefinitionHandler.java`

| Attribute | Default when absent |
|---|---|
| `address@length` | `1` (byte) |
| `address@bit` | `-1` (no bit extraction) |
| `conversion@endian` | **BIG** |
| `conversion@storagetype` | unsigned int of `length*8` |
| `gauge_min/max/step` | looked up **by units string** |

### 1.3 Default gauge ranges keyed on the units string

`ConverterMaxMinDefaults.java` — steal this table wholesale; it makes a new parameter render sensibly with zero configuration:

```java
add("%",       0.0, 100.0,  10.0);   add("f",     0.0, 400.0, 40.0);
add("c",     -20.0, 200.0,  20.0);   add("psi",  -20.0,  40.0,  5.0);
add("bar",    -1.5,   3.0,   0.5);   add("rpm",      0,  8000, 1000.0);
add("mph",     0.0, 200.0,  20.0);   add("km/h",   0.0, 300.0, 20.0);
add("degrees",-15.0, 60.0,   5.0);   add("g/s",    0.0, 400.0, 20.0);
add("v",       0.0,   5.0,   0.5);   add("ms",     0.0, 100.0, 10.0);
add("afr",    10.0,  20.0,   1.0);   add("lambda", 0.5,   1.5,  0.1);
add("gear",    0.0,   6.0,   1.0);   add("mmHg",   0.0,2000.0,100.0);
// fallback: min 0.0, max 100.0, step 10.0
```

### 1.4 `parameter` vs `ecuparam` — the actual distinction

From the official Logger XML Reference Guide (`https://www.romraider.com/RomRaider/LoggerXMLReferenceGuide`):

- **`<parameter>`** = a *well-known, manufacturer-documented* PID. One address, valid across all ECUs on that protocol. Availability is gated by **capability bits**: `ecubyteindex` + `ecubit` index into a bitmask the ECU returns at init. If the bit is 0, RomRaider **hides the parameter from the list entirely**. This is a great UI convention: don't show what this ECU can't produce.
- **`<ecuparam>`** = an *extended / reverse-engineered* RAM address that differs per ECU calibration ID. It carries `<ecu id="...">` children, each with its own `<address>`. RomRaider matches the connected ECU's ID and picks the right address. Conventionally named with a `*` suffix in the UI.

```xml
<ecuparam id="E2" name="Engine Load*" desc="">
    <ecu id="1B04400405"><address length="2">0x21847</address></ecu>
    <ecu id="4304594005"><address length="2">0x200F2</address></ecu>
    <conversions>
        <conversion units="g/rev" expr="x*.00006103515625" format="0.00"/>
    </conversions>
</ecuparam>
```

`group` / `subgroup` / `groupsize` batch several ecuparams into **one** memory read — the release notes say *"Group individual DS2 ECU queries into a single memory read start address"*. Exactly your 252-byte block problem.

### 1.5 Derived parameters — `<depends>` / `<ref>`

Computed channels with no address of their own. This is how you build "is this byte × RPM = something meaningful?" experiments:

```xml
<parameter id="P200" name="Engine Load (Calculated)" desc="...">
    <depends>
        <ref parameter="P8"/>   <!-- Engine Speed -->
        <ref parameter="P12"/>  <!-- MAF -->
    </depends>
    <conversions>
        <conversion units="g/rev" expr="(P12*60)/P8" format="0.00"/>
    </conversions>
</parameter>

<parameter id="P202" name="Manifold Rel. Pressure (Corrected)">
    <depends><ref parameter="P7"/><ref parameter="P24"/></depends>
    <conversions>
        <conversion units="psi" expr="[P7:psi]-[P24:psi]" format="0.00"/>
    </conversions>
</parameter>
```

Note `[P7:psi]` — reference another parameter **in a specific unit**. Cyclic dependencies are the author's problem ("Be careful of cyclic dependencies!" is a literal comment in the file).

### 1.6 Expression language

`JEPUtil.java` uses **JEP** (Java Expression Parser) with `addStandardFunctions()` + one custom function:

```
BitWise(Number mask, Number variable, Number operation)
  operation: 1=AND, 2=OR, ...   mask must be DECIMAL (0x18 fails to parse)
  e.g. BitWise(24, x, 1)
```

Real usage from the MS41 def: `BitWise(8,x,1)/8` → extract bit 3 as 0/1. `!BitWise(32,x,1)/32` → inverted bit 5. Variable is always `x`.

### 1.7 `<replace>` — the discrete lookup escape hatch

```xml
<conversion units="status" expr="x" format="0">
    <replace value="8"  with="Closed Loop"/>
    <replace value="10" with="Open Loop"/>
</conversion>
```

Parsed into a `Map<String,String>` applied *after* conversion. For enum-ish bytes (gear, fuel system status) this beats a formula.

### 1.8 ROM-side definition (`ecu_defs.dtd`)

`https://github.com/RomRaider/RomRaider/blob/master/definitions/ecu_defs.dtd`

```dtd
<!ELEMENT scale ( unit+ ) >
<!ATTLIST scale storagetype (uint8|int8|uint16|int16|float|hex|char) "uint8" >
<!ATTLIST scale endian (big|little) "big" >
<!ATTLIST scale logparam IDREF #IMPLIED >     <!-- links a ROM table to a live logger param! -->

<!ELEMENT unit EMPTY >
<!ATTLIST unit to_real CDATA #REQUIRED >      <!-- raw -> human -->
<!ATTLIST unit to_byte CDATA #REQUIRED >      <!-- human -> raw (inverse!) -->
<!ATTLIST unit format CDATA "0.00" >
<!ATTLIST unit coarseincrement CDATA "1" >
<!ATTLIST unit fineincrement CDATA "0.1" >
```

**Two formulas, forward and inverse** (`to_real` / `to_byte`, or `expression` / `to_byte` in `<scalingbase>`). Any editable field needs both. Also `fineincrement` should equal "the smallest change the raw value will accept" — i.e. one LSB expressed in engineering units.

`<scalingbase>` defaults (from the Editor XML Reference Guide, `https://www.romraider.com/RomRaider/EditorXMLReferenceGuide`): `expression="x"`, `to_byte="x"`, `format="#.##"`, `coarseincrement=2`, `fineincrement=1`, `min=0.0`, `max=0.0`.

```xml
<scalingbase name="engineSpeedRpm" units="RPM" expression="x*.1953125" to_byte="x/.1953125"
             format="#" fineincrement="50" coarseincrement="100" />
```

### 1.9 Logger UI, profiles, learning tables

Live data table columns (`LiveDataTableModel.properties`): **`Logger Data | Min Value | Current Value | Max Value | Units`**. Min/max are session-accumulated — free "what range does this byte actually cover?" instrumentation. Steal this.

Gauge labels (`PlainGaugeStyle.properties`): `min`, `max`, `Warn`, `above`/`below`.

**Profiles** (`profile.dtd`) — the logging profile is just a per-parameter set of three independent checkboxes:

```dtd
<!ATTLIST parameter livedata ( selected ) #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST parameter graph    ( selected ) #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST parameter dash     ( selected ) #IMPLIED >
<!ATTLIST parameter units    CDATA #IMPLIED >   <!-- remembers unit choice -->
```

Tabs: Data / Graph / Dashboard, plus tool tabs (Dyno, Injector, MAF). Menu: `Load Profile / Save Profile As`, `Tools → Learning Table Values`.

**Learning tables** are *not* a definition-file feature — they're hardcoded readers (`DS2FlkcTableQueryBuilder.java`) that generate one query per cell over a contiguous RAM block:

```java
final String addrStr = String.format("0x%06X", flkcAddr + (i * dataSize));
```

and split queries per row "to avoid maxing out the ECU send/receive buffer". Results render as a labelled grid (`Adaptation Table Values`, axes = Engine Load mg/stroke × Engine Speed RPM) with `Save to File` / `Save as Image`.

---

## 2. TunerPro RT

Help system root: `http://tunerpro.net/WebHelp/` (individual pages under `/WebHelp/source/`).

### 2.1 XDF item General tab — the canonical field set

`http://tunerpro.net/WebHelp/source/XDFConstantEditor.htm`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Title / Description / Units | display |
| **Address** | hex, offset by XDF header `Base Offset` |
| **Size** | **in bits** (8/16/32) — not bytes |
| **Signed** | checkbox |
| **LSB First** | checkbox — "checked for Intel, unchecked for Motorola" |
| **Output Type** | Floating Point / Integer / Hex Digits / String |
| **Significant Digits** | decimals for float; zero-padding width for int |
| Category A/B | two-axis tagging, used for filtering |
| **Use Low/High Range** | if enabled, input is *truncated* to range |
| **Visibility Level** | progressive disclosure by "knowledge level" |

Flags (`XDFFlagEditor.htm`): Address + **Bit Number, zero-based (0..7)**. That's it.

Tables (`XDFTableEditor.htm`) add: **Cell Data Size (bits)**, **Populate By** (row-major vs column-major), rows/cols counts, per-axis Units + Label Type + explicit label lists.

### 2.2 The conversion engine — genuinely worth stealing

`http://tunerpro.net/WebHelp/source/genconv.htm`

Operators: `* / + - %` and bitwise `| & ^`, plus parentheses. Any alpha character is an **argument**, and each argument is independently bound to one of **three source types**:

1. **This Item's Raw Data** (default)
2. **Other XDF Item Output** — the *converted* output of another item
3. **Raw Value at Address** — arbitrary address + **size in bits** + **endianness (1 = LSB first, 0 = MSB first)**

Worked examples straight from the docs:

```
(1.35 * X) - 40                 ; temperature, X = this item's raw data
0.351567 * (X - Y)              ; X = raw data, Y = raw value at bias address
(0.351567 * X) - Y              ; X = raw data, Y = another XDF item's output
```

Note `X * X` is legal and the two X's are *not* necessarily the same value — argument identity is positional, not by name.

### 2.3 Real XDF XML (v1.60)

Verified against `https://github.com/saildot4k/MSS54-XDFs` (BMW MSS54) and `https://github.com/jaytektas/PIS/blob/master/delco.xdf`.

```xml
<XDFFORMAT version="1.60">
  <XDFHEADER>
    <flags>0x1</flags>
    <deftitle>MSS54 v2801 E30 Swap Items</deftitle>
    <author>Justin Ooms</author>
    <BASEOFFSET offset="0" subtract="0" />
    <DEFAULTS datasizeinbits="8" sigdigits="2" outputtype="1"
              signed="0" lsbfirst="0" float="0" />
    <REGION type="0xFFFFFFFF" startaddress="0x0" size="0x8000"
            regionflags="0x0" name="Binary File" desc="..." />
    <CATEGORY index="0x13" name="Contains Alpha-N map (DKBA)" />
  </XDFHEADER>

  <XDFCONSTANT uniqueid="0x1D4C" vislevel="1">
    <title>Sport Mode_MEMORY</title>
    <description>...</description>
    <CATEGORYMEM index="2" category="66" />
    <EMBEDDEDDATA mmedaddress="0x4024" mmedelementsizebits="8"
                  mmedmajorstridebits="0" mmedminorstridebits="0" />
    <units>"-"</units>
    <outputtype>2</outputtype>
    <datatype>0</datatype>
    <DALINK index="0" />
    <MATH equation="x"><VAR id="x" /></MATH>
  </XDFCONSTANT>

  <XDFFLAG uniqueid="0x7C09">
    <title>Two Stroke</title>
    <EMBEDDEDDATA mmedaddress="0xF004" mmedelementsizebits="16" />
    <mask>0x1</mask>
  </XDFFLAG>

  <XDFPATCH uniqueid="0x544A">
    <title>Disable SAP/CAT Heating/DTC</title>
    <XDFPATCHENTRY name="SAP" address="0x75D4" datasize="0x6" patchdata="00FF04B0B9B9" />
    <XDFPATCHENTRY name="DTC" address="0x7BBE" datasize="0xE" patchdata="AA010101010101000102032800FF" />
  </XDFPATCH>
</XDFFORMAT>
```

A table is `<XDFTABLE>` containing three `<XDFAXIS id="x|y|z">`, each with its own `EMBEDDEDDATA`, `indexcount`, `<MATH>`, and optional static `<LABEL index= value=/>`. `<min>`, `<max>`, `<decimalpl>`, `<rangehigh>` sit on the axis.

**`mmedtypeflags` bitfield decode** — authoritative, from RomRaider's `XDFConversionLayer.java` (`src/main/java/com/romraider/xml/ConversionLayer/XDFConversionLayer.java`):

```
0x01  signed
0x02  LSB first (little-endian);  clear => big-endian
0x04  swap X/Y (row/column-major flip)
```

`mmedmajorstridebits` / `mmedminorstridebits` are the row/column strides **in bits** — negative values are legal (see the `-32` in the MSS54 y-axis above), which lets you walk a table backwards. That's a nice trick if your byte layout is reversed.

**There is no published XDF spec document.** The format is only documented through the WebHelp UI descriptions above; everyone else reverse-engineers it. Best executable references: `RomRaider/XDFConversionLayer.java`, `https://github.com/bri3d/a2l2xdf` (A2L→XDF generator), `https://github.com/willemml/xdftuneparser-rs`, `https://github.com/whalenlg/xdf_parser`.

### 2.4 ADX — the live-datastream format (this is your actual analogue)

TunerPro splits *bin definition* (XDF) from *datastream definition* (ADX/ADS). ADX is what you want to copy.

**ADX Value** (`http://tunerpro.net/WebHelp/source/DADefValue.htm`):

| Field | Note |
|---|---|
| Title, **Unique ID** (max 15 chars, referenced by lists/dashes/histograms) | |
| Data Type + Stock Units | *optional*, used only to auto-link to XDF items |
| **Units Override** | what's actually displayed |
| **Packet Offset (H \| D)** | zero-based byte index into the packet — **dual hex/decimal input fields side by side** |
| **Data Source Size** | bits |
| **Signed**, **LSB First** | |
| **Range Low / Range High** | raw limits, used by "Percentage of defined range" output |
| **Alarm High / Low + enables** | value renders red bold when breached |
| Command Association | which request this value arrives in |

Conversion tab: same equation engine, but argument types are only **Native** (raw at this offset) or **Linked Output** (another ADX Value). Then optionally **"Send converted data to lookup table"**.

Output formats: Hex, Integer, Unsigned Integer, Floating Point, **Percentage of Defined Range** (`[current - min] / [max - min]`). Truncation, never rounding.

**ADX Lookup Tables** (`DADefLookup.htm`) — a first-class calibration primitive, list of (input, output) pairs with four **Lookup Modes**:

| Mode | Given entries `[2.0→4.0]`, `[4.0→8.0]`, input 2.5/3.0/3.5 |
|---|---|
| **Interpolate** | 5.0 / 6.0 / 7.0 |
| **Closest** | 4.0 / 8.0 / 8.0 |
| **Previous** | 4.0 / 4.0 / 4.0 |
| **Next** | 8.0 / 8.0 / 8.0 |

Clamps at both ends; exact input matches always bypass the mode. There's a **Table Graph tab where you drag points with the mouse**. This is exactly the right UI for "I have 40 samples of raw byte vs. known ground truth, fit me a curve."

**ADX Bitmask** (`DADefBitmask.htm`): offset, size, LSB First, **Operation = bitwise AND or XOR** against an operand, then **Display on TRUE** / **Display on FALSE** strings + alarm-on-true/false. Not a bit *index* — a mask plus an operator.

**ADX Header** (`DADefHeader.htm`): Baud (1200–921600), **RS232 Echo** (discard local echo — matters on K-line), and three command slots: **Connection Command**, **Monitor Command** (sent in a loop), **Disconnect Command**. Commands are Send / Listen / **Macro** (an ordered group, typically send+listen).

Packets are modelled as **fixed-size header + body + footer**; the payload lives in the body, and packet offsets are relative to it.

**Data Acquisition Tracing** (`DATracing.htm`) is the killer feature: link the XDF to the ADX, then while streaming, **the live value lights up the currently-active cell in the ROM table**. Axis labels must be numeric, not strings, for this to resolve.

---

## 3. WinOLS

Vendor: `https://www.evc.de/en/product/ols/software/`

### 3.1 Automatic map detection — the heuristics

Vendor claims: *"Automatic processor recognition to distinguish between program and data area"*; *"Program code, empty areas, maps etc. are automatically detected. An overview window shows what can be found where in the file. Program code and empty areas are automatically displayed in pale."*

Reported detection criteria (`https://ecufiles.io/technik/winols-map-erkennung`):

1. **Statistical distribution analysis** to separate code from data (machine code has a distinct byte histogram).
2. **Axis monotonicity** — runs of *strictly monotonically increasing* values, ~8–32 elements, in plausible numeric ranges, flag a candidate axis.
3. **Smoothness / second derivative** — maps have low second derivatives; noise has high ones throughout.
4. **Value-range plausibility** per candidate data type (uint8/int16/…); reject regions of all-`0xFF` or all-`0x00`.
5. **Known-ECU database matching** for recognised binaries.
6. **Cross-version differencing** — the most reliable method: two calibrations of the same ECU *"differ almost exclusively in the map regions"* because code is identical.

Corroborating visual description (`https://www.fileservice24.at/en/blog/winols-guide-finding-maps`): code is *"chaotic, high-frequency noise with no discernible pattern"*; maps are *"smooth, structured shapes: gentle curves, clean staircases, ramps that rise and plateau, or flat lines."*

### 3.2 Visual conventions

- Raw data shown as **2D graphic OR hex/decimal dump**, switchable, plus **3D chart**, **table**, and (5.46+) **"Slices"** — all lines drawn at the same height so shapes can be compared.
- **Overview window**: whole-file map, code and empty regions greyed pale.
- **Preview window**: free-floating, resizable, renders the *current selection* as a live 3D map. This is the key interaction — the 3D preview updates as you drag the selection, and a coherent shape is the confirmation signal.
- Four preset colour schemes, user-configurable.

### 3.3 Manual map definition — actual keystrokes

From the HP Academy WinOLS course (`https://www.hpacademy.com/courses/winols-mastery-map-identification-and-editing/`):

| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Increase / decrease display width (columns) | **M** / **W** |
| Shift alignment by one byte (remove the green vertical guide line) | **Ctrl + arrow keys** |
| Select the map region | click-drag from left of the data; drag edges to fine-tune |
| **Convert selection into a defined map** | **K** |
| Open properties | double-click the map |
| Reuse scaling | right-click → **"copy map properties"**, untick *"data source plus address"*, **Ctrl+V** onto the next map |

Properties dialog fields: Name/Description, Units, **Data Type** (e.g. *"16 bit high low"* — endianness is part of the type name), **Factor** and **Offset**.

Axis linking for 3D maps is done from the hex view, *before* creating the map:
- right-click the first Y value → **"address as Y axis of the next map"**
- right-click the first X value → **"address as X axis of the next map"**

Axes can differ in width from the Z data (16-bit axis + 8-bit map data is common); switching the view between 8/16-bit is how you tell whether an axis is real — *"the second axis just becomes complete garbage"* in the wrong width.

Typical factors seen in the wild: `/4096` for relative fill %, `/327.68` for throttle % (16-bit full-scale 0–100), `×40` for RPM, `/128` for lambda.

Also relevant: **`File → Import → Map Pack / Damos / A2L`** (import known definitions), **`File → Compare with File`**, an **XDF importer plugin** (`https://www.evc.de/en/product/ols/xdf_importer.asp`), and a **LUA scripting** plugin.

## 4. ECUFlash

XML format, real example (`https://github.com/Crowley2012/SubaruTuning/blob/master/Definitions/ECUFlash/subaru/Forester%202.5/EP5D201D.xml`):

```xml
<rom>
  <romid>
    <xmlid>EP5D201D</xmlid>
    <internalidaddress>2004</internalidaddress>
    <internalidstring>EP5D201D</internalidstring>
    <ecuid>7112346007</ecuid>
    <year>2011</year> <market>USDM</market> <make>Subaru</make>
    <memmodel>SH7058</memmodel>
    <checksummodule>subarudbw</checksummodule>
    <flashmethod>subarucan</flashmethod>
  </romid>
  <include>32BITBASE</include>

  <scaling name="Advance(degrees)2" units="Advance (degrees)"
           toexpr="(x*.001525879)-40" frexpr="(x+40)/.001525879"
           format="%.2f" min="0" max="50.00" inc=".5"
           storagetype="uint16" endian="big" />

  <table name="Primary Open Loop Fueling Cruise" address="cd35c">
    <table name="X" address="cd308" elements="13" />
    <table name="Y" address="cd33c" elements="8" />
  </table>
</rom>
```

Full table forms (from `https://github.com/dparrish/ecurom/tree/master/xml/ecuflash`):

```xml
<table name="ALS minimum vehicle speed to trigger" category="Turbo"
       address="1e12" type="1D" level="1" scaling="VehicleSpeed"/>

<table name="ALS Air injection time" category="Turbo" address="4e3a"
       type="2D" level="1" scaling="Timesecbyte">
    <table name="RPM" address="7792" type="X Axis" elements="9" scaling="RPM"/>
</table>

<table name="Fuel Map 1 - HI OCTANE" category="Fuel and Ignition Maps"
       address="118A3" type="3D" swapxy="true" scaling="AFR">
    <table name="Load" address="2eb42" type="X Axis" elements="10" scaling="Load"/>
    <table name="RPM"  address="2ec62" type="Y Axis" elements="15" scaling="RPM"/>
</table>
```

Table `type` values observed: `1D`, `2D`, `3D`, `X Axis`, `Y Axis`, `Static X Axis`, `Static Y Axis`. `storagetype` values: `uint8`, `int8`, `uint16`, `int16`, plus **`bloblist`** — the enum/selection editor:

```xml
<scaling name="blobbits" storagetype="bloblist" storagebits="1">
    <data name="0" value="00"/>
    <data name="1" value="01"/>
</scaling>
```

**Relationship to RomRaider — they are near-isomorphic, and converted in both directions in production:**
- The Subaru file above is literally stamped *"This file was generated by RR2EcuFlash version: 1.0.0.33977"* (RomRaider → EcuFlash).
- `<include>32BITBASE</include>` is EcuFlash's inheritance; RomRaider uses `<rom base="32BITBASE">`.
- Attribute mapping: EcuFlash `toexpr`/`frexpr` ⇄ RomRaider `expression`(`to_real`)/`to_byte`; `inc` ⇄ `fineincrement`; `format="%.2f"` (printf) ⇄ `format="0.00"` (DecimalFormat). `storagetype`, `endian`, `address`, `elements`/`size` are identical in spirit.
- Converters in the wild: `https://github.com/Switchleg1/xdf2xml`, `https://gist.github.com/guicho271828/dbb4195df9316fd37e333eb9b828fde3`, and RomRaider's own `XDFConversionLayer.java` / `VDFConversionLayer.java` / `BMWCodingConversionLayer.java`.

Discovery methodology on the EcuFlash side is *disassembly*-driven, not statistical (`https://evoecu.logic.net/wiki/Locating_Tables`): find calls to the shared axis-lookup routine `sub_CC6`, read the axis header (result pointer, input-value pointer, length word, then data), then the table header carries a **dimension marker (0x2 = 2D, 0x3 = 3D)** plus a global offset. Different problem from yours, but the *header-describes-shape* idea is worth noting.

## 5. Firmware hex-diff / differential analysis tooling

### Domain-specific

| Tool | What it gives you | URL |
|---|---|---|
| **TunerPro Comparison Tool** | Best-documented model. Pick 2 of 5 loaded bins (1 editable + 4 compare buffers), enter **start/end address range**, checkbox **"limit to items defined in the XDF"**. Output = one row per differing byte; **undefined bytes rendered in blue**; click → locate in list, double-click → open editor. Explicitly notes a 2-byte item shows as 2 rows. | `http://tunerpro.net/WebHelp/source/DiffTool.htm` |

Diffs two binaries into a portable **`.remap` recipe** capturing every changed byte **plus 32 bytes of context anchors** so the patch survives firmware revisions. Confidence-scored ECU identification (30 extractors, Bosch/Siemens/Delphi/Marelli). | `https://github.com/v-arapidis/openremap-core` |
| **romHEX14** | A2L-aware ROM-to-ROM comparison, **map-by-map in physical units** rather than raw bytes. | `https://romhex14.com` |

### General-purpose (better UI ideas)

- **ImHex** (`https://imhex.werwolv.net/`) — pattern language, data inspector, **file diffing**, and visualizers: **entropy, digram, byte distribution**. The digram/entropy plots are the closest open-source analogue to WinOLS's code-vs-data overview.
- **radare2 `radiff2`** — `-c` byte count, `-s` similarity/distance, `-x` hex-column diff.
- **VBinDiff** (`https://www.cjmweb.net/vbindiff/`) — two-pane synchronised scrolling hex with differences highlighted; tiny and the interaction model is trivially copyable.
- **binvis.io / Veles** — space-filling-curve and trigram binary visualisation; good for "where is the structured region".
- **bsdiff / xdelta / Kaitai Struct / 010 Editor binary templates** — for the record.

### Also worth stealing from an adjacent field

Your actual problem — *N unknown bytes streaming at low rate, find which one is TPS* — is the **CAN signal-identification** problem, which has better-published algorithms than the ECU-tuning world. Relevant prior art: **READ** (Reverse Engineering of Automotive Data frames), **LibreCAN**, **CAN-D**, and **SavvyCAN**'s sniffer view, which highlights *changed bytes since last frame* with per-byte colour decay and offers a "signal finder" that correlates candidate bit-ranges against a reference channel. That colour-decay-on-change hex grid is probably the single highest-value widget for your UI.

## 6. Direct hit for your E36 — RomRaider's BMW MS41 DS2 logger definition

RomRaider release notes: *"BMW DS2 protocol implementation for MS41, MS42 and MS43 DME"*, *"DS2 protocol now supports 'Telegram', logging arbitrary addresses, requires a new logger definition v352 or later"*.

Definition file (v354, DS2-only, 89 `ecuparam`s, covering ECU IDs `1405854, 1406464, SHINDE1, 1429373, 1429861, 1432401, 1437806, 1440176`):
`https://github.com/0x000NULL/tuning/blob/main/BMW/MS41%20Logger%20Definitions.xml`

**The two you're looking for:**

```xml
<ecuparam id="P13" name="..TPS" desc="Throttle Position (STATUS_DROSSELKLAPPEN)"
          group="0x0B" subgroup="0x01" target="1">
    <ecu id="1405854,1429373,1429861,1432401,1437806,1440176">
        <address>0x0000E8D7</address>
    </ecu>
    <ecu id="1406464,SHINDE1">
        <address>0x0000E8D0</address>   <!-- TPS Post Adaptation -->
    </ecu>
    <conversions>
        <conversion units="%" expr="x*100/255" format="0.0"
                    gauge_min="0" gauge_max="100" gauge_step="10" />
    </conversions>
</ecuparam>

<ecuparam id="P9" name="/VS" desc="Vehicle Speed (STATUS_GESCHWINDIGKEIT)"
          group="0x0B" subgroup="0x01" target="1">
    <ecu id="1405854,1406464,SHINDE1,1429373,1429861,1432401,1437806,1440176">
        <address>0x0000DA63</address>
    </ecu>
    <conversions>
        <conversion units="km/h" expr="x" format="0" gauge_min="0" gauge_max="300" gauge_step="30" />
        <conversion units="mph"  expr="x*0.621371192" format="0.0" gauge_min="0" gauge_max="250" gauge_step="25" />
    </conversions>
</ecuparam>
```

So: **TPS = `0xE8D7`, uint8, `x*100/255` %** and **road speed = `0xDA63`, uint8, `x` km/h (raw = km/h, 1:1)**.

Cross-check against your five knowns — these are the same file:

| Addr | Name | Type | Expr | Units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0xDA2A` | RPM | uint16 | `x` | RPM |
| `0xDA34` | MAF | uint16 | `x*0.25` | kg/h |
| `0xDA50` | IAT | uint8 | `x*0.747-48` | °C |
| `0xDA5A` | ECT (coolant) | uint8 | `x*0.747-48` | °C |
| **`0xDA63`** | **Vehicle Speed** | **uint8** | **`x`** | **km/h** |
| `0xDAA5` | Atmospheric Pressure | uint8 | `101.325*37/255` | psi |
| **`0xE8D7`** | **TPS** | **uint8** | **`x*100/255`** | **%** |
| `0xE8DE` | TPS Adaptation | int16 | `x*1.526E-3` | % |
| `0xE989` | Ignition | uint8 | `0.373*x-23.6` | °BTDC |
| `0xE98D` | Knock | uint8 | `(x-128)*0.375` | ° corr |
| `0xE9E6` | VANOS | uint8 | `x*0.3745` | KW° |
| `0xEF7E` | IPW (injection pulse width) | uint16 | `x*0.00534` | ms |
| `0xF01E`/`0xF030` | STFT1 / LTFT1 | uint16 | `(x-32768)*100/65535` | % |
| **`0xFAFC`** | **Load** | **uint16** | **`x*0.0212`** | **mg/stroke** |
| `0xF141` | Compressor relay | uint8 | `!BitWise(32,x,1)/32` | On/Off |

Battery voltage appears as an **ADC pseudo-channel** (`V_Batt`, `x*0.102` VDC) rather than a RAM address, so if your battery-volts byte is in the 252-byte window, your window may be a different block than these — but note **coolant, IAT and RPM all live in `0xDA2A–0xDA5A`**, a ~50-byte span. A 252-byte window starting near `0xDA00` would contain RPM, MAF, IACV, IAT, ECT, **vehicle speed (`0xDA63`)**, knock sensors and atmospheric pressure — but **not TPS**, which is 3.6 kB higher at `0xE8D7`, and not Load at `0xFAFC`. If your window does contain injection load, it isn't the `0xDA00` block. Worth resolving before you build anything: dump your window's base address and check it against this table.

Companion definitions for the other Siemens BMW DMEs: `https://github.com/Rustle333/Siemens-MS43`, `https://github.com/Rustle333/MSS52`, `https://github.com/Rustle333/M5.2`.

## 7. What to actually steal for your UI

**Data model** — one `Parameter` with N `Conversion` children:

```
Parameter { id, name, desc, address, length=1, bit=-1, group/subgroup }
Conversion { units*, expr*, format*, storagetype?, endian?=big,
             gauge_min?, gauge_max?, gauge_step?, replace[] }
```

Everything else is optional with a defaulting rule. RomRaider's exact set, and it's the smallest schema that covers all five known-good channels above.

**Nine conventions, ranked by value to your discovery problem:**

1. **Min / Current / Max columns, session-accumulated** (RomRaider live data table). Free range discovery on every unknown byte at once — a byte that has covered 0–255 is not coolant temp.
2. **Default gauge ranges keyed on the units string** (§1.3). Type "km/h", get a 0–300 axis. Zero-config plausibility checking.
3. **Change-highlighted hex grid with colour decay** (SavvyCAN sniffer / WinOLS 2D view). At 1 Hz over 252 bytes this is the primary instrument: idle the engine, blip the throttle, watch which cell flashes.
4. **A live 3D/2D preview slaved to the current selection** (WinOLS preview window). Shape coherence is the confirmation signal — a monotone ramp when you sweep the throttle *is* the proof.
5. **Adjustable display width + one-byte alignment nudge** (WinOLS `M`/`W` and `Ctrl+arrow`). You don't know the stride; make it a slider, not a config field.
6. **Interactive lookup table with 4 modes and a draggable graph** (TunerPro ADX). Plot raw byte vs. ground truth from a scan tool, drag points, get a conversion. Far better than making the user guess `a*x+b`.
7. **Derived/computed channels via `depends`+`ref`** (RomRaider). Lets the user test hypotheses — "byte 47 × 0.5 minus byte 12" — without touching code. Reference other params *in a chosen unit*: `[P7:psi]`.
8. **Bit-level items as first-class citizens**, both styles: TunerPro's `mask` + AND/XOR + TRUE/FALSE labels, and RomRaider's `bit` index + `BitWise(mask, x, op)`. Road speed on some ECUs is packed; switches definitely are.
9. **Capability gating and visibility levels** — hide what this ECU can't produce (RomRaider `ecubyteindex`/`ecubit`), and tier by confidence (TunerPro `vislevel`, RomRaider `userlevel 1–5`). For a discovery tool, repurpose this as a **confidence field**: `confirmed / probable / guess / unknown`, and colour the hex grid by it.

**Two more, specific to your workflow:** adopt RomRaider's `*`-suffix convention to mark reverse-engineered vs. documented parameters, and store the unit selection in the saved profile (`profile.dtd` `parameter@units`) so a session reload doesn't lose the user's calibration choices.
