# EFI Tuning Dashboards & Log Analysis — Feature Research

## 1. TunerStudio MS (EFI Analytics) — the reference implementation

### 1.1 Editions and what gates behind them

The [TunerStudio 3.1 Feature Matrix](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/119-tunerstudio-30-feature-matrix) is the single most useful inventory of features. Verbatim rows:

**Free (Lite):** Basic Data Logging · Contextual Help Bubbles · Editing of all Controller Settings · Firmware Loader · Ignition & Composite Logger display · Load and Save Tune Files · Main Dash Selectable Gauges · Multiple Project Support · Offline tuning · Table 3D Tuning Dialog · Unlimited Length Logging

**Registered adds:** Add Channel Wizard (Simple) · Advanced Math Functions · Bluetooth Direct / FTDI D2XX USB / WiFi comms · Compare Tune to saved tune · Contextual Settings Notes · Curve Graph Baselines · Curve Graph Tools · CurveGraph Multi-Select · **Dashboard Designer** · **Data Log Profiles** · **Data Log Triggering - Auto Logging** · Enhanced 2D Table · Enhanced 3D Tuning · GPS Support · **Graphical Difference Reports** · **High Speed (>15Hz) Logging** · Ignition & Composite Logger *File load* · **Multiple Tabbed Dashboards** · Notes Log · Performance and Economy Fields · Recent Project List · **Settings Search** · Single Dialog Settings Save/Load · **VE Analyze Live - Auto Tune** · **WUE Analyze - Warm up Auto Tune**

**Ultra adds:** **Integrated Log Viewer** · **Log Trailing and Playback** · **Trim Table AutoTune** · **Tuning & Dyno View Designer** · **Tuning & Dyno Views** · Channel Editor (Simple & Advanced) · **X-Y Plotting on Curve Graphs** · **Full Application Log Playback** · **Trigger Sound Alerts** · **User Actions** · **Action Triggers** · **Acceleration Performance Dash**

Note the design signal: the *analysis* and *automation* features are what people pay for. Basic gauges are free.

### 1.2 The gauge object model — extracted from real `.dash` files

This is the highest-value finding. TunerStudio `.dash` files are XML (`<dsh xmlns="http://www.EFIAnalytics.com/:dsh">`). I downloaded and parsed several real ones (e.g. `MS3_Sweep.dash`, `MS4PPC_Analog_Bar.dash` from [bryhasagithub/arduino-afr-gauge](https://github.com/bryhasagithub/arduino-afr-gauge/tree/master/tuner-studio-dashes)). Every gauge is a `<dashComp type="Gauge">` with this **complete** property set:

**Value / scale**
- `Min`, `Max` — scale endpoints
- `LowCritical`, `LowWarning`, `HighWarning`, `HighCritical` — the four band thresholds
- `MinVP`, `MaxVP`, `LowCriticalVP`, `LowWarningVP`, `HighWarningVP`, `HighCriticalVP` — **"ValueProvider" variants: every limit can be an expression, not a constant.** Real examples found: `loadhigh`, `prefSpeedUnits == 0 ? 200 : 300`. This means gauge redlines can follow the tune's own config values instead of being hardcoded.
- `DefaultMin`, `DefaultMax` — restore points
- `PegLimits` (bool) — clamp the needle at the endpoints rather than letting it fly off-scale
- `ValueDigits`, `LabelDigits` — decimal places for the readout vs. the axis labels separately
- `Units` — also expression-capable (`bitStringValue( prefSpeedUnits, prefSpeedUnits )`), so a gauge relabels itself psi/bar/kPa from a preference

**Peak-hold / ghost needle (the "min/max memory" feature)**
- `ShowHistory` (bool) — enables the peak marker
- `HistoricalPeakValue` (double) — the retained peak
- `HistoryDelay` (int, ms) — **15000 by default**; how long the peak marker lingers before decaying back

**Damping**
- `NeedleSmoothing` (int) — needle damping factor
- `SmoothedValue` — the damped value actually rendered, kept separate from raw `Value`

**Geometry (arc gauges)**
- `StartAngle`, `SweepAngle`, `SweepBeginDegree`, `FaceAngle` (180 or 360), `CounterClockwise` (bool), `DisplayValueAt180` (bool)
- `MajorTicks`, `MinorTicks` — `-1.0` means auto

**Appearance**
- `BackColor`, `FontColor`, `TrimColor`, `NeedleColor`, `WarnColor`, `CriticalColor` (all ARGB)
- `BackgroundImageFileName`, `NeedleImageFileName` — per-gauge images
- `FontFamily`, `ItalicFont`, `FontSizeAdjustment`, `AntialiasingOn`, `BorderWidth`, `RelativeBorderWidth2`, `Insets`

**Layout**
- `RelativeX`, `RelativeY`, `RelativeWidth`, `RelativeHeight` — **all normalized 0..1**, which is why dashes are resolution-independent across a laptop and a 7" Pi screen
- `ShapeLockedToAspect` (bool) — per-gauge aspect lock
- `GroupId` — grouping for multi-select ops
- Layout manager is `com.efiAnalytics.tunerStudio.GaugeClusterLayout`

**Behavior**
- `OutputChannel` — the bound data channel
- `ShortClickAction` / `LongClickAction` — **tap actions per gauge** (found in the wild: `toggleDatalogging`). Distinct short vs. long press.
- `RunDemo` (bool) — **demo mode: the gauge animates with fake data so you can design a dash with no car attached.** Underrated feature.
- `InvalidState`, `GoingDead`, `MustPaint` — explicit stale/dead-data states, so a gauge can visually indicate "this number is no longer live" rather than silently freezing

### 1.3 The actual gauge styles

Extracted `GaugeStyle` / `GaugePainter` values across real dash files — this is the complete built-in set:

| Style name | Renderer class |
|---|---|
| Analog Gauge | `AnalogGaugePainter` |
| Circle Analog Gauge | `RoundAnalogGaugePainter` |
| Asymetric Sweep Gauge | (sic — misspelled in the product) |
| Analog Bar Gauge | `AnalogBarPainter` |
| Analog Moving Bar Gauge (High CPU) | `AnalogMovingBarGaugePainter` |
| Horizontal Bar Gauge | `HorizontalBarPainter` |
| Vertical Bar Gauge | `VerticalBarPainter` |
| Vertical Dashed Bar Gauge | `VerticalDashedBarPainter` |
| Horizontal Line Gauge | (line/sparkline style) |
| Histogram | `HistogramPainter` — **a rolling mini-histogram as a gauge widget** |
| Basic Readout | `BasicReadoutGaugePainter` — plain numeric |

Indicators are a separate component type (`<dashComp type="...Indicator">`) with two painters: **`RectangleIndicatorPainter`** and **`BulbIndicatorPainter`**. Indicator properties: `OnText`/`OffText`, `OnTextColor`/`OffTextColor`, `OnBackgroundColor`/`OffBackgroundColor`, `OnImageFileName`/`OffImageFileName`, `Insets`, `Painter`. Note the design: an indicator always has a **label in both states** ("WUE off" / "WUE ON"), not just a light that's on or off — you can always read what it monitors.

Per [Dashboard Enhancements](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/98-dashboard-enhancements): "Individual Background Images for every gauge", "Separate On and Off Images for Indicators", and critically **"All Images are saved to the .dash file, so 1 file contains the whole dash"** — fonts too (I confirmed embedded base64 TTFs, e.g. Arial Black, inside `MS3_Sweep.dash`). Single-file portability was a deliberate goal.

### 1.4 Dashboard Designer — how users actually compose a dash

From [Using TunerStudio Dashboard Designer](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/support/manuals/53-using-tunerstudio-dashboard-designer):

- Enter via **right-click anywhere on the dashboard → "Designer Mode"**. No separate app, no mode toolbar — the dash itself becomes editable in place.
- Full WYSIWYG drag-and-drop placement.
- **CTRL+Click** to multi-select; selected items show **"a yellow X"** with resize handles.
- **Tab key cycles through stacked gauges by Z-order** — solves the "gauge is buried under another gauge" problem.
- Right-click → **"Gauge Styles → {choice}"** to restyle a selection.
- Right-click → **"Properties → Gauge Colors → Font Color"**, **"Properties → Gauge Text"**.
- Gauge limits dialog: right-click → **"Dashboard Designer → Properties Dialog → Gauge Limits & Values"** ([source](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/62-changing-gauge-limits)) with fields Minimum / Maximum / Low Warning / High Warning / High Critical. On a tachometer, **High Warning renders as the yellow line and High Critical as the red line**.
- Designer mode shows a **grid and live coordinate readout** for alignment.
- TS 3.0 consolidated things: "Most Designer mode Properties are now bundled into a single dialog for easier access", and added **click actions** (open a settings dialog or table, reset a channel, start/stop datalogging, send a controller command) with **separate single-click and long-click assignments**.
- Aspect ratio lock exists both per-gauge (`ShapeLockedToAspect`) and dash-wide ("forced aspect ratio support at fullscreen" per the [change log](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/downloads/tschangelogmenu)).

**Named layouts per task**: this is the **"Multiple Tabbed Dashboards"** feature — you add as many dashboards as you want, each a tab, and switch between them. Combined with Action Triggers you can auto-switch dashboards on a condition (see 1.6).

**Fullscreen "in-car" mode**: TunerStudio has a "make dashboard fullscreen" preference (a paid feature). The [rusEFI Digital Dash TunerStudio guide](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/wiki/Digital-Dash-TunerStudio) documents the in-car recipe: Raspberry Pi 3B+/4, 7" monitor, enable "load last project on startup" + "make dashboard fullscreen", and it boots straight into a dash.

### 1.5 Tuning & Dyno Views — the best idea in the product

[Tuning and Dyno Views](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/114-tunerstudio-tuning-and-dyno-views) (Ultra) generalizes the dashboard into a **task-specific composite workspace**. You "build your own views with pretty much any set of gauges and settings you want on a single tab". Components you can drop in:

- **Settings Panel** — an embedded panel lifted out of a normal menu dialog
- **Tuning Table** — a table or curve graph, no scrollbars, freely resizable
- **Gauge Cluster** — a region of gauges
- **Table Cross Cell Cross Hair** — a widget showing *which cell you are currently operating in* and how centered you are in it
- **Burn Button** — commit-to-flash control

Saved as individual **`.tuneView`** files, shareable across projects and machines. Shipped examples: **Dyno Pull View** (huge AFR readout + main fuel table + targeting widget + temp gauges), **Fuel Table View** (2D + 3D fuel table + cell targeting), **AE Settings View** (accel enrichment settings + gauges).

This is the direct answer to "idle tuning dash vs WOT dash vs diagnostic dash": the good version isn't just different gauges, it's *gauges + the exact settings panel + the exact table you're editing, on one screen, per task.*

### 1.6 Alerting: Action Management

[Action Management](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/125-action-management) (Ultra) splits into **Action Triggers** (a condition expression, or an ECU digital input, fires an action) and **User Actions** (parameterized actions you define once and reuse, bindable to a trigger *or* to a dashboard gauge click).

Built-in actions: Exit and Shutdown (closes project, exits TS, cleanly shuts down the OS) · Browse Projects · Create New Project · **Mark Dialog** ("Place a Mark in the data log if one is being captured") · **Move to Dash on Left** / **Move to Dash on Right** (wraps around) · Start Data Logging (auto-names by date/time) · Stop Data Logging · Toggle Data Logging.

User Action targets: Execute a Shell Command · Load Tune or Partial Tune (`.msq` / `.msqpart`) · **Mark Data Log Comment** (adds a mark *with a text comment*) · Open a Project · **Play a Sound** (WAV/MP3) · Reset Runtime Value (trip meters, accumulated distance) · Send Controller Command (e.g. engine kill) · **Show Global Warning** ("Displays a message regardless of what screen or tab you are on that must be dismissed") · **Show Passive Message** (lower-left corner notification) · Show Settings Dialog.

The two-tier warning model is worth stealing: **Global Warning = modal, must dismiss** vs **Passive Message = corner toast**. Plus audible alerts as a first-class action.

Per [this msextra thread](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=72539), the practical guidance from EFI Analytics' Phil Tobin: "Most of the TS/SD dashes have indicators at the bottom. In designer mode you can put them anywhere you want, as big or small as you want." Right-clicking an indicator lists every indicator the firmware `.ini` declares; anything else requires creating your own OutputChannel.

### 1.7 Custom channels and the math parser

Menu path: **Tools → Custom Channel Editor** ([Add Channel Editor and Wizard](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/115-tunerstudio-add-channel-wizard)). Three creation modes:
1. **Linear Sensor** — pick input channel + two known calibration points
2. **Non-Linear Sensor** — input channel + an `.inc` file of value↔output pairs
3. **Advanced Expression** — arbitrary formula over any OutputChannel or calibration value

Page 2 of the wizard then lets you emit a **Gauge Template** (appears in every dashboard's right-click gauge menu) and/or a **DataLog Field** (gets logged automatically). Persisted to `custom.ini`. Example given: `status1 & 32 ? 1 : 0` (bit test → boolean channel, i.e. how you make a custom indicator lamp).

The [Math Parser Functions](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/support/manuals/88-math-parser-functions) list is extensive. Grouped:

- **Trig/log/exp**: `sin cos tan asin acos atan log log10 exp pow(val,exp) sqrt recip`
- **Rounding**: `round floor ceil abs`
- **Time-series (the interesting ones)**:
  - `smoothBasic(field, smoothingFactor)` — moving average over N records
  - `smoothFiltered(val)` — matrix filter, **reduced lag** vs plain averaging
  - `lastValue(anyField)` / `historicalValue(anyField, n)` — previous / n-back record
  - `minValue(field, TimeToReset[opt])` / `maxValue(field, TimeToReset[opt])` — **running min/max with optional auto-reset window; this is the peak-hold primitive**
  - `accumulate(expr)` / `persistentAccumulate(expr)` — running sum; the persistent variant survives across sessions (odometers, fuel used)
  - `timeToExceed(target, expr, timeExpr[opt])` — measures time until a target is reached (0-60 style)
  - `timeTrue(boolExpr)` — seconds a condition has been continuously true
  - `isTrueFor(boolExpr, seconds)` — **debounce: returns false until the condition holds for N seconds.** This is exactly how you avoid alarm flicker.
  - `toggle(boolExpr, initialState[opt])` — latch flip-flop
  - `updateValueWhen(reEvalExpr, expr)` — sample-and-hold
- **Aggregates**: `min(...)`, `max(...)`, `sum(...)` (Excel-style, N args)
- **Conditional**: `if(cond, then, else)`, `selectExpression(index, e0, e1, ...)`, plus C ternary `cond ? a : b`
- **Table lookup**: `table(expr, 'file.inc')`, `tableLookup([array.values],[array.lookup],[channel])` (interpolated 1D), `tableLookup([z],[x],[y],[xCh],[yCh])` (2D), `arrayValue(Constant, indexExpr)`
- **Domain-specific physics**: `accelHp(velocityMPH, deltaV, deltaT, weightLb)`, `aerodynamicDragHp(v_ms, airDensity, Cd, frontalArea_m2)`, `rollingDragHp(speedMPH, tirePressurePsi, weightLb)` — **built-in virtual dyno math**
- **App/runtime**: `timeNow()`, `systemTime()`, `getLogTime()`, `isOnline()` (1 if connected to ECU), `isNaN(val)`, and a family of `getChannel*ByOffset()` reflection helpers

MegaLogViewer's variant ([formulas.html](http://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewerHD/formulas.html)) uses bracket field references with historical indexing: `[RPM]` = current, **`[RPM-1]` = previous record**. Operators: `+ - / * ^ ~ & | % >> >>> << !`, comparators `== != >= <= > <`, logical `&& || AND OR`, ternary `{cond} ? {a} : {b}`. Important gotcha documented verbatim: **"Math is executed from left to right, operation hierarchy is not recognized."** Parentheses are mandatory for precedence. Menu path: **Calculated Fields → Custom Fields → Add Custom Field**; names are case-sensitive and must be unique.

What people actually compute (from the product's own marketing): **RPM/Sec** (rate of change for detecting pulls), **Vacuum**, **Boost** (MAP minus baro), **PW-1**, AFR error (target minus actual), Z-delta between two fields.

TunerStudio also ships **Performance and Economy Fields** ([source](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/92-performance-and-economy-fields)): aerodynamic drag, net horsepower, net torque, rolling drag, distance traveled, MPG/MPL/KPL, cc/min, gal/hr, lb/hr, instantaneous consumption. Requires a speed channel from the ECU or a **10 Hz GPS**.

### 1.8 Data logging

**Data Log Profiles** ([source](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/94-data-log-profiles)) — menu **Data Logging → Data Log Profiles**. Named subsets of channels. UI is a two-list shuttle (Logged / Not Logged) with `<` and `>>` buttons for single and bulk moves. A "Default Data Log Profile" contains everything and is not editable. You can hold multiple profiles per project and switch between them while the dialog is open; Accept commits. **Fewer channels = higher sample rate** on firmware that supports partial reads.

**Automatic Logging** ([source](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/93-automatic-logging)) — menu **Data Logging → Automatic Logging**. Enable checkbox top-left, then independent start and stop conditions. Simple mode: channel dropdown + `>` `=` `<` + value. Advanced mode: select "Expression" and write a full formula. Documented example: `rpm < 2500 && tps < 50`. If start is automatic and stop is manual, it records until you stop it or the engine shuts down.

**High Speed Logging** ([source](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/95-high-speed-logging)) — >100 records/sec on MS3/MS3-Pro v1.3+, 75+ on MS2Extra 3.3+. Achieved by *chunked reads* (splitting requests) and newer protocol extensions that read only the needed bytes in one call, at 115200 baud.

**Markers.** Confirmed mechanics: press **spacebar during live logging** to drop a mark; on Android/ShadowDash, **double-tap the screen** ([msextra](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=45929)). Action Management can also place a mark **with a text comment**. Rendering in MegaLogViewer, from its [change log](http://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewer/changeLog.html): *"Display log file MARKS recorded by Megatune"* (v0.9.8) and **"Red lines in status bar to indicate MARK positions"** (v2.611) — i.e. marks appear as red ticks on the scrub/position bar, so you can see and jump to them at a glance across the whole log. Known gap users complain about: **SD-card logging has no marker support**; the community workaround is "two quick WOT blips after the event - pretty easy to find in the data logs."

The binary `.mlg` (MLVLG) format carries markers as a distinct block type. Confirmed in [mlg-converter](https://github.com/karniv00l/mlg-converter): block type `0` = field record, block type **`1` = `marker`**. Its README warns: "MLVLG also carries data type called Markers (graphical marks used for indicating specific events). They **will be stripped** in .csv files."

### 1.9 Composite / tooth / trigger logging

The best writeup is DIYAutoTune's [Using the Tooth Logger and Composite Logger](https://www.diyautotune.com/support/tech/using-the-tooth-logger-and-composite-logger/). Menu: **Diagnostics & High Speed Loggers** tab, logger type dropdown on the left.

**Tooth Logger** — a single row of vertical bars; each bar's height is the *time between consecutive crank pulses*. Reading it:
- equal bars = steady RPM; shortening = accelerating; lengthening = decelerating
- a bar split into two halves = a **noise pulse** between real teeth
- a double-height bar = a **missed tooth**
- a missing-tooth wheel shows a repeating pattern with a tall bar at the gap

**Composite Logger** — three stacked traces over time: **green (top) = cam / secondary**, **blue (middle) = crank / primary**, **red (bottom) = sync-loss flag**. Thin spikes = single-edge detection; square waves = both edges captured. Red bars mid-log = loss of sync — and the caveat that "the problem may occur up to two crank rotations before the flag appears."

Capture workflow: pick logger type → tick **"Capture to log file"** → name it → Start → run the engine through the problem range → Stop. Critical UX failure they document: **"If you do not click the box to capture a log to a file, you can't save it after recording."** That's a textbook mistake to avoid — never make recording a pre-declared mode when you could just keep a ring buffer and let people save retroactively.

Buffer behavior: fixed page size; the logger rolls to a new page after a fixed time unit. In Speeduino's `.ini` (`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/sp.ini`, from [speeduino.ini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noisymime/speeduino/master/reference/speeduino.ini)), `[LoggerDefinition]` declares four `loggerDef` entries: `"Tooth Logger"` (type `tooth`, 127 entries × 4 bytes), `"Composite Logger"`, `"Composite Logger 2nd Cam"`, `"Composite Logger Both cams"` (type `composite`, 127 records × 5 bytes). Composite record fields: `priLevel`, `secLevel`, `ThirdLevel`, `trigger`, `sync`, `cycle` (1 bit each) + `refTime` (32-bit, 0.001 ms scale). Derived: `calcField = toothTime, "ToothTime", "ms", { refTime - pastValue(refTime, 1) }`.

rusEFI's version ([tunerstudio.template.ini](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/blob/master/firmware/tunerstudio/tunerstudio.template.ini)) is richer — its composite log also carries **`cam1`–`cam4`, `coil1`–`coil8`, `inj1`–`inj8`, and `TDC`** as flags, giving you a full digital timing diagram of inputs *and* outputs on one time axis. It additionally defines a third logger type: **`loggerDef = triggerScope, "Trigger Oscilloscope", csv`** with two 8-bit **analog voltage channels** scaled `{6.6 / 255}` volts — an actual scope on the raw trigger wires, for diagnosing VR sensor waveform problems that a digital logger can't see.

### 1.10 Integrated Log Viewer and Full Application Playback

This is the "dashboard replays with the cursor" behavior you asked about, and it's explicitly confirmed by EFI Analytics' own Phil Tobin on the forum:

> "TunerStudio displays the line graphs that are on MLV's 1st tab and in the beta, will play the log back throughout the application. So all your dashboard gauges will read and table traces will work based on the log playback." — [msextra thread](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=122&t=72275)

[Full Application Log Playback](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/126-log-playback): "When you load a log file, you can not only view it in the integrated Log Viewer, but now all the data in the log will be displayed throughout TunerStudio." It **simulates a live vehicle connection** — dashboards, gauges, table traces, and the cell crosshair all animate from the log as if the car were running.

[Integrated LogViewer](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/products/tuner-studio/tsarticles/113-tunerstudio-integrated-logviewer-1): "view your logs and **trace log values to any table or 1d curve setting in the system**" — i.e. scrubbing the log moves a marker across your VE table showing which cell the engine was in at that instant.

**Log Trailing** = live tail: the viewer follows a log file as it is being written, so you can analyze the beginning of a pull while the end is still recording.

Change log entries confirming related behavior: "Added support for **multiple loaded logs**", "Added **Multi-Log bar** to allow fast switching between compare logs", "Added support for **tracing on 3D tables during log playback**", "**Playback of HighSpeed & Ignition Logs**", "View in MegaLogViewer will start as trail and playback", "1D tables show the interpolated value in the tool tip".

### 1.11 Auto-tune from logs

**VE Analyze Live** (Registered) — live, while driving. Marketing: "As you drive, VE Analyze Live will look at all the data, filter out the junk, and use weighted statistical averages to calculate the optimal values for your fuel tables." Features named on the product page: **automatic update to controller**, **heat maps showing data coverage and changes**, **authority limits to prevent damage**, standard + custom parameter filters, and **Lambda Delay compensation**.

The Lambda Delay table is the key concept: exhaust takes time to reach the O2 sensor, and that time varies enormously with RPM and load — at idle it can be many times longer than at high RPM. Without it, "the wrong cells are being tuned."

**Offline VE Analyze in MegaLogViewer** ([veAnalysis.html](http://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewer/veAnalysis.html)) — load a log **plus** the matching `.msq` tune, pick the VE table, click **"VE Analyze"** then **"Run Analysis"**. Output: a suggested table where each cell shows **hit count** and **weighting**, with the original value in the tooltip. "The higher the weighting the more sure you can be that optimal value has been generated" — low-weight cells stay anchored to their original value. Settings:
- **Cell Change** — resistance; set to "Hard" and the original value is respected more strongly, requiring stronger evidence to override
- **Wide band delay** — "If set to 1 the AFR value from x+1 will be used when processing record x"; useful range 0–2
- **Wideband O2 AFR** source selector
- Filters: **Min RPM / Max RPM / Min MAP / Max MAP / Min CLT / Start Time / Stop Time / Custom Filter** (expression, e.g. `[RPM] > 2000 && [TP] > 80`)
- **Right-click a cell to revert it individually or hand-edit before accepting the table**

The firmware declares the filter set itself. Speeduino's `[VeAnalyze]` block declares: `std_xAxisMin`, `std_xAxisMax`, `std_yAxisMin`, `std_yAxisMax`, `std_DeadLambda` (auto-built), plus `minCltFilter` ("Minimum CLT", default 71°C / 160°F), `accelFilter` ("Accel Flag", bit test `engine & 16`), `aseFilter` ("ASE Flag", `engine & 4`), `overrunFilter` ("Overrun", `pulseWidth = 0`), and `std_Custom`. rusEFI's adds `deltaTps > 50`, `VBatt < 12`, `minTps < 1`.

The design lesson: **the filters are named after the physical reason data is untrustworthy** (accel enrichment active, afterstart enrichment active, decel overrun, engine cold, dead lambda), not after abstract statistics.

**WUE Analyze** (warm-up enrichment auto-tune) uses the same architecture on a 1D curve, with `maxTPS > 15`, `minRPM < 300` filters. **Trim Table AutoTune** (Ultra) does individual cylinder trims — "so you don't even need to have a Wideband for every cylinder."

### 1.12 Other TunerStudio features worth noting

- **Settings Search** — search across all settings by name. Essential given hundreds of dialogs.
- **Graphical Difference Reports** — side-by-side comparison of two tunes with visual diff; also automatic **restore points** created on project close and on configuration changes.
- **Contextual Help Bubbles** and **Contextual Settings Notes** — per-setting notes saved *inside the tune file*, so a tuner's rationale travels with the tune.
- **Curve Editor** (3.0): multi-select cells, increment/decrement blocks, **interpolate from 2 points**, copy/paste blocks, **baselines** (ghost of a reference curve), a **floating ellipse tracking the current run point**, and Ultra's **X-Y plotting** to overlay any logged channel pair onto the curve.
- **Acceleration Performance Dash** (Ultra): 0–30 / 0–60 / 0–100 MPH, and drag-strip style 60ft / 330ft / 660ft / 1320ft / 5280ft each with **time and speed**, viewable and loggable ("Write Timeslip data to mlg log files").
- Menu structure (from [useasydocs](http://www.useasydocs.com/TunerStudioMS/TSmenu.html)): File · Options (Language, Look and Feel, Navigation, Advanced, Preferences, **Performance** — gauge animation, dialog modes, lite mode) · Datalogging (Start Logging CTRL-L, Stop CTRL-B, **Burst Logging Mode**, Import/Conversion, View with MegaLogViewer) · Communications (Settings, **Data Rate**, Mini-Terminal, Diagnostic Log Comm) · Tools (Binary Log Viewer, **Expression Evaluator**, Calibrate TPS, Calibrate Thermistor Table) · Help. Note there is a dedicated **Performance** options page purely for gauge animation cost — a real concern on a Raspberry Pi.

## 2. MegaLogViewer / MegaLogViewer HD — log analysis specifics

Sources: [efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewerHD](https://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewerHD/), [classic MLV](http://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewer/), [histograms.html](http://www.efianalytics.com/MegaLogViewerHD/histograms.html).

**Navigation and keyboard** (this is the in-the-weeds detail):
- Left/Right arrows — move **record by record**
- Page Up / Page Down — move a **graph page** at a time
- Home / End — jump to start / end of file
- Up / Down arrows — **zoom in / out**
- Dedicated Play / Stop / Speed keys for playback
- **Dragging on the time scale selects a range and yields averages over that range** — the single most useful analysis gesture in the whole tool: select a window, get mean values for every channel
- Marks render as **red lines in the status bar**

**Core analysis views:**
- **Standard log viewer** — stacked line graphs with a shared cursor
- **Compare mode** — "Overlay second file values"; plus a **Multi-Log bar** for fast switching among several loaded logs
- **Playback** with speed control
- **View any 16 grouped Replay Signals** — a digital/bit-flag lane view (16 boolean channels grouped together), for status bits
- **Table cells marked for each record** — as you scrub, the corresponding VE/spark table cell highlights
- Handles "hundreds of thousands of records"; supports 30+ log formats (MegaSquirt, EFI Live, HP Tuners, Haltech, Motec, AEM, Holley EFI, Cobb, ECUMaster, Power Vision, plus generic CSV/delimited and binary)

**Histogram / Table Generator** — the killer feature. You "select any field for your X, Y and Z axis and instantly have a table generated with statistics on the data." Specifics:
- X and Y axes fully customizable (usually RPM × MAP to mirror the VE table)
- Z = the value being aggregated (AFR, spark, VE)
- **Z Delta** mode = difference between two fields, i.e. **AFR target minus AFR actual per cell — an error map**
- **Filters toggle on and off with near-instant re-render** — this interactivity is what makes it usable
- Adjustable row/column count; **setting rows to 1 turns it into a bar chart**
- Uses: "see how far off every cell of your fuel table is by processing all the data in your logs", "plot your spark or AFR table to see where knock is occurring"
- Also has an **"Import from loaded Tune"** button to pull axis breakpoints from the actual tune

**3D Scatter Plots** — X vs Y with a third variable encoded, for finding correlations (there's a MegaMeet 2013 presentation "Tuning With Scatter Plots" by Phil Tobin, referenced [here](https://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/support/manuals/103-tuning-with-scatterplots-presentation-megameet-2013), PDF hosted at DIYAutoTune).

**Custom Calculated Fields** and **advanced custom data filters** as described in 1.7.

**Offline Auto Tuning** (VE Analyze) as described in 1.11.

## 3. Speeduino

Speeduino ([github.com/noisymime/speeduino](https://github.com/noisymime/speeduino), now also `speeduino/speeduino`) has **no dashboard software of its own** — it ships a TunerStudio `.ini` and the `.ini` *is* the dashboard contract. Docs at [wiki.speeduino.com](https://wiki.speeduino.com).

The `.ini` (6062 lines) sections that define the UI: `[GaugeConfigurations]`, `[FrontPage]`, `[OutputChannels]`, `[Datalog]`, `[LoggerDefinition]`, `[VeAnalyze]`, `[WueAnalyze]`, `[Tools]`, `[CurveEditor]`, `[TableEditor]`, `[Menu]`, `[SettingContextHelp]`, `[ControllerCommands]`, `[EventTriggers]`.

**Gauge declaration format** — this is the minimal viable gauge schema, and it's worth copying:

```
; Name   Var   Title   Units   Lo   Hi   LoD   LoW   HiW   HiD   vd   ld
tachometer = rpm, "Engine Speed", "RPM", 0, {rpmhigh}, 300, 600, {rpmwarn}, {rpmdang}, 0, 0
```

with the comments defining semantics exactly: `LoD` = "Lower limit at which **danger** color is used for gauge background", `LoW` = "Lower limit at which **warning** color is used", `vd` = decimals in the displayed value, `ld` = decimals in the Lo/Hi scale labels. Note **the thresholds can be `{expressions}`** referencing tune constants (`{rpmwarn}`, `{maphigh}`, `{12 / 14.7 * stoich}`).

Gauges are organized by **`gaugeCategory`**: `"Main"`, `"Sensor inputs"`, `"Auxiliary Input Channels"`, `"System Data"`. Categories drive the right-click gauge picker menu, which is how you make ~120 gauges navigable.

Nice touches in Speeduino's set: `mapGauge` / `mapGauge_psi` / `mapGauge_bar` / `mapGauge_vacBoost` (in-Hg below atmospheric, PSI above — one gauge that reads correctly on both sides of atmospheric), a `#if CELSIUS / #else` block giving different limits per unit system, `syncLossGauge` (# sync losses, warn at 10, danger at 50), `loopGauge` / `loopSmoothGauge` (main loop speed, **danger below 750 loops/s** — a health gauge for the ECU itself), `memoryGauge` (free RAM), `TPSdotGauge` / `MAPdotGauge` (rate-of-change channels).

The `[FrontPage]` default cluster is a 4×2 grid: tachometer, throttle, pulse width, duty cycle / MAP, IAT, CLT, gamma enrichment.

### Standard indicator lamps (Speeduino) — the full list

This directly answers "what are the standard indicator lamps". Format is `{expression}, "off-label", "on-label", off-bg, off-fg, on-bg, on-fg`:

**Engine state:** Running · Cranking · ASE ON (afterstart enrichment) · WUE ON (warmup enrichment) · Accel · Decel · MAP Accel · MAP Decel · ERROR · FLOOD CLEAR (`(tps > tpsflood) && (rpm < crankRPM)`) · DFCO On (decel fuel cutoff) · Idle ON

**Limiters and cuts (all red):** Launch Hard · Launch Soft · Soft Limiter · Hard Limiter · Ign Cut (Boost) · Nitrous On · Staging On

**Sync (the diagnostic trio):** Full Sync (green) · **Half Sync (yellow)** · No Sync — three states, not two

**Engine protection (all red):** Engine Protect ON · Rev Limiter ON · Boost Limit ON · Oil Pres. Protect ON · AFR Protect ON · Coolant Protect ON

**Faults:** I/O Error · VVT1 Error · VVT2 Error · WMI Tank Empty · Battery Voltage Warning (`(batteryVoltage < batlow) || (batteryVoltage > bathigh)` — a two-sided check on one lamp)

**System:** EEPROM Burn (pending write) · Reset Lock ON · Custom Boot · Fan ON · A/C Request / A/C Comp / A/C Fan · Programmable out 1–8

**SD card:** SD Present · SD ready · SD Logging · SD Error

Color convention is consistent and worth adopting: **green = a normal function is active**, **red = something is being cut, limited, protected, or has failed**, **yellow = degraded/partial** (half sync), **white = inactive**.

rusEFI's equivalent set adds: Config Error · **Unsaved changes** (yellow — `needBurn`) · Warning · Trigger ERR · dynamic text indicators like `{ Fuel cut: bitStringValue(fuelIgnCutCodeList, fuelCutReason) }` — **the lamp label itself renders the *reason* for the cut**, which is far better than a generic "fuel cut" light. Also Clutch Up/Down, Brake down, Idling, Coasting, TPS/TPS2/Pedal/CLT/IAT/Flex error, ETB RPM Limit, WBO state machine lamps (Preheat / Warmup / Closed loop / Heating failed / Overheat / Underheat), **"Tuning Detected"**, and SD "ECU Mode" vs "PC Mode".

## 4. rusEFI

### 4.1 The rusEFI console (Java/Swing)

Actual tab list, read from [`ConsoleUI.java`](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/blob/master/java_console/ui/src/main/java/com/rusefi/ConsoleUI.java): **Gauges · Messages · Lua Scripting · Engine Sniffer · Live Data · Tuning · Knock Analyzer · SLCAN Sniffer · Pinout · Manage Tunes**. Commented out in source (historical): Log Viewer, LE controls, ADC, ECU stimulation, live map adjustment, Wizards, Settings.

Official description ([wiki](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/wiki/Console), [forum thread](https://rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=263)): "a handy monitoring, development and debugging tool… The most useful feature is the plain signal sniffer — both real inputs and generated signals can go into it… Another useful feature is the text log. You can use the console to invoke rusEFI commands and control the internal flow using the 'Messages Central' tab." With the built-in position sensor emulator it allows bench testing "without a real engine or any additional hardware." Author's own assessment: "This console is pretty plain, but still… This tool is not intended to replace the 3rd party tuners."

**Gauges tab mechanics** (from `GaugesPanel.java` / `GaugesGridElement.java` / `SensorGauge.java`):
- A **grid of gauges with user-selectable rows × columns**, chosen via a `SizeSelectorPanel` popup — the Excel "drag to pick a 3×4 grid" interaction
- Each grid cell can be **either a round gauge or a live strip graph**, toggled by right-click → **"Switch to Live Graph"** / **"Switch to Gauge Mode"**
- **Double-click a gauge to detach it into its own floating window** (`DetachedSensor`) — tooltip literally says "Double-click to detach / Right-click to change"
- Right-click opens a **menu nested by `gaugeCategory`** from the `.ini`, listing every gauge by title
- Gauge rendering uses the **SteelSeries** Java library (`eu.hansolo.steelseries.gauges.Radial`). Notably `setThresholdVisible(false)` — rusEFI does *not* draw warn/danger bands, just a red pointer. This is a visible quality gap vs TunerStudio.
- Gauge titles and units can be **expressions resolved live** from the ECU (e.g. a Lua gauge renaming itself)
- There is a global `IS_PAUSED` flag — a freeze-the-gauges control
- Live graph right-click menu: **Scale → Auto scale / Use custom lower / Use custom upper**, and **Refresh period → 3 seconds / 1 second / second / 5 / second / 10 / second / 20**

### 4.2 rusEFI logging

[Logging Guide](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/wiki/Logging-Guide):
- Format is **`.mlg`**, MegaLogViewer-compatible, from both TunerStudio and SD card ("the content between the two methods differs slightly, but all important fields are identical")
- TunerStudio: `Data Logging → Start Logging`, default filename is a date/time stamp, **a green indicator appears at the bottom of the dashboard while active**, `Data Logging → Stop`
- **Data rate: 100 Hz recommended**; "Max reads per second" exists for trigger-sync analysis but "will make a humongous log file pretty quickly"
- SD logging: `Controller → SD Card Logger`, "Enable SD Card" = true, default write interval **50 ms (20 Hz)**, ~**20 MB/hour**, ~400 hours on an 8 GB card
- USB/power sequencing determines mode: powered by vehicle first → logging mode; powered by USB first → mass-storage/transfer mode
- Community norm: upload logs to **rusEFI Online** rather than posting screenshots — "a proper log file is almost always the first thing you will be asked for"

[Diagnostics and Logging](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/wiki/Diagnostics-and-Logging) names the trigger toolset: **engine sniffer, composite logger, tooth logger**, plus a **rusEFI Virtual Simulator** to "exercise the firmware and console on a PC without any hardware."

### 4.3 rusEFI digital dash options

[Digital Dash](https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/wiki/Digital-Dash) lists five: TunerStudio on Raspberry Pi · PowerTune on RPi3 · custom clusters (uaDash, PiDGC) · Android apps (**RealDash, Shadow Dash, MSDroid**) · **combo10** (10" touchscreen, customizable gauge layout, engine-config wizard, limited on-device tuning).

Two constraints stated that any in-car dash designer should internalize:
> **"a dash that takes thirty seconds to appear is a dash that is blank every time you start the car"** — boot time is a feature

and that hardware must survive "heat and shakes." Most dashes read **CAN broadcast** — one-way, so the dash can't corrupt the ECU.

## 5. FreeEMS and the open-source alternatives

### 5.1 FreeEMS ecosystem

[freeems-vanilla](https://github.com/fredcooke/freeems-vanilla) deliberately did *not* use the MegaSquirt protocol: "FreeEMS remains the only original free and open source ECU with its own bespoke, documented, standardised, and open protocol and associated tuning software. The other two both use, or at least used to use, the Megasquirt protocol and proprietary tuning software." That decision cost it TunerStudio compatibility and, arguably, the ecosystem.

Its tools:
- **[EMStudio](https://github.com/fredcooke/emstudio)** — "Cross Platform FreeEMS tuning application, written in c++ with Qt" (Qt4 + Qwt + QJson + OpenGL). README is refreshingly blunt: "thrown together in an impressively short time frame and has all of the maintenance and quality issues associated with proof-of-concept development style. Right now, it's your only choice for live tuning FreeEMS." Windows unsupported: "likely to be similarly painful to having toe nails removed with pliers." Plugin architecture — see `emstune-freeems`.
- **[OpenLogViewer (OLV)](https://github.com/gufi/OpenLogViewer)** — Java log grapher, reads FreeEMS binary logs and MegaSquirt-compatible logs. Its UI vocabulary (from `Labels.properties`) is instructive:
  - **"Divisions"** — the log canvas splits into horizontal lanes; each division holds one or more traces. "Add Division" / "Click Here to remove this division and associated Graphs". This is the stacked-plot concept made explicit and user-editable.
  - Per-field **Min Value / Min Display / Max Value / Max Display** — the *data* range and the *display* range are separate, so you can zoom a channel's Y-axis without touching others. Hint text: **"To modify Min and Max values for scaling purposes Ctrl+LeftClick"**.
  - **"Reset Min/Max"** button
  - Menus: File (Open, **Open last**, Quit) · View (**Full Screen**, **Scale And Color**, **Fields And Divisions**) · Options (Add New Property, Remove Selected Properties) · Help
  - An **FPS counter** in the UI (`FramesPerSecond = FPS:`) and explicit out-of-memory handling with messages like "Detected impending out-of-memory doom!" — performance on huge logs was the dominant engineering problem
- **[freeems-tuner](https://github.com/srynot4sale/freeems-tuner)** (wxPython), **[fuct](https://github.com/MrOnion/fuct)** (FreeEMS Unified Console Tools), **[freeems-loader](https://github.com/seank/freeems-loader)**, **[freeemssim](https://github.com/fredcooke/freeemssim)** (hardware/software simulator)

### 5.2 HyperTuner — the modern web reimplementation (most relevant reference)

[hyper-tuner/hypertuner](https://github.com/hyper-tuner/hypertuner) (127★) and [hypertuner-cloud](https://github.com/hyper-tuner/hypertuner-cloud) (79★, live at [hypertuner.cloud](https://hypertuner.cloud)). Supports Speeduino, rusEFI, FOME. Stated goals include "clean, intuitive, modern and responsive UI", "fast startup and low resource consumption", "easy for newcomers with tips, tools and simple diagnostics."

Concrete implementation details worth copying (React + TypeScript):
- Charts use **[uPlot](https://github.com/leeoniya/uPlot)** — canvas-based, built for hundreds of thousands of points
- **`uPlot.sync('logs')`** with `cursor.sync: { key: plotSyncKey }` — **synchronized cursor across multiple stacked plots**. Hovering one chart moves the crosshair on all of them. This is the "cursor-linked charts" mechanic implemented in ~1 line.
- `cursor.drag: { y: false }` — **drag selects a time range on X only** (never accidental Y zoom)
- Three zoom plugins: `mouseZoomPlugin`, `touchZoomPlugin`, **`keyboardZoomPlugin`** — touch matters because people use tablets in cars
- Y-scales keyed by **units** (`scale: field.units`) — channels sharing a unit automatically share an axis, which is the right default for a 70-channel log
- Channel picker uses **Fuse.js fuzzy search** with debounce, and there are **two independent field-selection panels** feeding two stacked charts, plus a `showSingleGraph` toggle
- Log parsing runs in a **Web Worker** (`logParserWorker`) with a **progress percentage** — the log is 50 MB and nobody should stare at a frozen tab
- Separate components for `CompositeCanvas` and `ToothCanvas` (trigger logs), with **`PAGE_SIZE = 200`** pagination; composite traces are drawn as offset square waves (primary translated by 1, secondary by 2.6, scale 2) with a separate `sync` trace
- There is a **`CommandPalette.tsx`** — Cmd-K style navigation, which is the modern answer to TunerStudio's "Settings Search"
- A **Diagnose** page separate from Logs and Tune

Companion: **[mlg-converter](https://github.com/karniv00l/mlg-converter)** — MIT-ish Node/npm parser for the binary `.mlg` format, converts to CSV/JSON/MSL, and there's an [mlg-wasm](https://github.com/karniv00l/mlg-wasm) build. If you're building anything that reads TunerStudio logs, start here rather than reverse-engineering the format.

### 5.3 UltraLog

[ultralog.co](https://ultralog.co/) — free ECU datalog viewer, supports 10 ECU manufacturers including Speeduino and rusEFI. Its feature list is essentially a modern spec sheet for what a log viewer should have:

- **Interactive Charts** — zoom, pan, multi-channel overlay, up to 10 simultaneous channels
- **Stacked Plots** — independent panels with separate Y-axes
- **2D Histogram Heatmaps** — interactive
- **Scatter Plot Correlation**
- **Synchronized cursor tracking across all channels**
- **Time-range selection** integrated with playback
- **Multi-file tab system** for side-by-side log comparison
- **Computed Channels** — "virtual channels with mathematical formulas **and time-shifting**" (time-shift is exactly the EGO-delay problem, generalized)
- **14 analysis algorithms** including AFR drift detection and statistical correlation
- **Min/Max Legend** — an overlay showing peak values per channel (the ghost-needle idea applied to charts)
- **Playback at 0.25x to 8x**
- Unit conversion across 8 categories with metric/imperial toggle
- **Colorblind-accessible palette**
- PNG and PDF export

### 5.4 RealDash

[realdash.net](https://realdash.net/) — Android/iOS/Windows/Linux, connects via USB / Bluetooth / WiFi, custom hardware via the **RealDash CAN** protocol. Marketing term for the editor is **"PixelPerfect™"** — bring your own graphics.

The [manuals index](https://realdash.net/manuals.php) reveals the model:
- **[Normal / Warning / Critical levels](https://realdash.net/manuals/using_normal_warning_and_critical_levels.php)**: every gauge has a **Range** (min/max clamp), a **Warning Level**, and a **Critical Level**, each with its own min/max, configured in the **"Input & Values"** popup. Colors are then set per-level under **"Look & Feel" → "Colors"** with a level selector. So the *same* gauge has three complete color schemes, not just a band on a dial. This generalizes warn/danger to numeric and image gauges, not only dials.
- **[Making an indicator](https://realdash.net/manuals/make_an_indicator.php)**: Add Gauge → **Image**, set background image, attach an input (e.g. Engine/ECU Inputs → Check Engine Light), then set the **Image Blend Color opacity** near-zero at Normal level so the lamp is "barely visible" when off and fully opaque at Warning/Critical. Elegant: one mechanism (per-level styling) produces both gauge bands and indicator lamps.
- **[Keyboard shortcuts](https://realdash.net/manuals/keyboard_shortcuts.php)** — a genuinely well-thought-out editor:
  - Edit mode: Ctrl+Z undo · Ctrl+X/C/V · Ctrl+A select all, Shift+Ctrl+A select none · Ctrl+O/S load/save dashboard · **align left/right/top/bottom = Ctrl+H/K/U/M** · **Ctrl+4 pixel perfect, Ctrl+5 fullscreen, Ctrl+7 match sizes** · Tab / Shift+Tab cycle gauges · arrow keys nudge
  - Run mode: **arrow keys switch pages** · F9 screenshot to gallery · **F4 fullscreen** · **F5–F8 switch aspect ratio presets** · Shift+6 enter edit mode · spacebar toggles menu
- Also has Data Multicast, Voice Commands, Music Player, and Recording Video.

Note the friction documented on the [Speeduino forum "Digital dash" thread](https://speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=2602&start=10): the RealDash developer had to special-case Speeduino because "RealDash does not understand the ochGetCommand of `r\$tsCanId\x30%2o%2c` in speeduino.ini file. It expects it to be 'A' for serial connections." Third parties parse the TunerStudio `.ini` but only support a subset of it.

### 5.5 ShadowDash MS

EFI Analytics' Android dashboard app ([customizing guide](http://www.tunerstudio.com/index.php/support/manuals/84-customizing-your-dashboards-in-shadow-dash-ms)):
- Ships **8 default dashboards per firmware family: 4 landscape and 4 portrait**
- **Page 1 is a home screen using gauges available on the phone itself** so it does something useful with no ECU connected — good idea for a dead-connection state
- Pages 2–3 are firmware-specific and user-replaceable; **Page 4 is generated from the `.ini` and always represents the default dash** (guaranteed fallback)
- Dashboards are the *same* `.dash` files authored in TunerStudio, dropped into `/Shadow Dash MS/[FirmwareFamilyProject]/dashboard/`
- Supports `custom.ini` for custom OutputChannels and gauge definitions, mirroring TunerStudio
- Marker gesture is **double-tap the screen**

[tunerstudiodashboards.com](https://tunerstudiodashboards.com/) is a community library of free `.dash` files (track, Ferrari/Audi/Supra-inspired, motorcycle, minimalist), plus **image packs for borders, indicators, gauge backgrounds and needles**. Its install guidance also names the real portability problem: "you may need to reassign the **Output Channel** for the gauges to the correct ECU outputs" — dashes break across firmware because channel names differ.

### 5.6 Other Speeduino dashboard projects

Mostly embedded, not web: [Brokenagain-motorsport/Speeduino-Dash](https://github.com/Brokenagain-motorsport/Speeduino-Dash) (LVGL + TFT_eSPI, 480×320), [amrikarisma/mazduino-display-speeduino](https://github.com/amrikarisma/mazduino-display-speeduino) (ESP32-C3 + ILI9488 3.5"), [DiogoSilvaK/Speeduino-Waveshare-Dashboard](https://github.com/DiogoSilvaK/Speeduino-Waveshare-Dashboard), [ric355/SpeedyLogger](https://github.com/ric355/SpeedyLogger) (bare-metal Raspberry Pi logger), [rob-deutsch/js-speeduino-comm](https://github.com/rob-deutsch/js-speeduino-comm) (Node serial library), [askrejans/speeduino-to-mqtt](https://github.com/askrejans/speeduino-to-mqtt), and importantly [askrejans/speeduino-serial-sim](https://github.com/askrejans/speeduino-serial-sim) — **a Speeduino protocol simulator with a realistic engine model, streaming over UART or WiFi TCP, explicitly for "testing dashboards, loggers, and ECU integrations without real hardware."** If you build a dashboard, this is how you develop it.

I found **no** project matching "Speeduino Universal Dashboard" or "SpeeduinoDash" as a vanilla-JS web dashboard — that niche appears genuinely unoccupied. HyperTuner is the closest thing and it's tuning-first, not dash-first.

## 6. What people complain about (UX mistakes to avoid)

### Documentation and discoverability
The dominant complaint by a wide margin.

> "Why does all the information for this megasquirt stuff always seem so hard to find? Must be that grocery store thing again… I keep thinking of VE analyze in tunerstudio and how easy it is to load a tune in it and cant believe its the whole grocery store thing again… So now im starting to get frustrated, you all know it." — [msextra, on being unable to find how to load a tune into MegaLogViewer HD's Histogram/Table Generator](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=65782)

> "Can someone direct me to a user manual or tutorial for MegaLogViewer? I can't seem to find anything useful in the help file or online." … "I assume that since the only references on the MLV site are a sales pitch for MLVHD and a blank users manual that this is all top secret stuff." — [msextra](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=100&t=66606)

> "Regarding instructions for MLVHD, there really aren't any. **The issue the program is it will work with so many ECUs all with different names for the same thing, it gets really confusing.**" — [msextra](https://www.msextra.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=66358)

That last one is the deep structural problem: supporting 30 ECU formats means the app can never name anything concretely, so every label is generic and every workflow is abstract.

### The two-apps problem
TunerStudio and MegaLogViewer are separate products with **overlapping but inconsistent** capability. The same operation (load a tune) works differently in each. TunerStudio Ultra's Integrated Log Viewer only covers "the line graphs that are on MLV's 1st tab" — scatter plots, histograms, custom calculated fields, and offline auto-tune remain MLV-only, so serious users must own and context-switch between both.

### Feature gating creates cliffs
The composite/tooth logger only functions in *registered* TunerStudio; log *display* is free but log *file loading* is not; the "make dashboard fullscreen" and "load last project on startup" options — the two settings you need to use it as an in-car dash — are paid. Users hit walls mid-task.

### Modal recording
"If you do not click the box to capture a log to a file, you can't save it after recording" (composite logger). You just did a diagnostic pull and the data is gone.

### Missing markers on the path people actually use
Spacebar markers work for PC logging; **SD-card logging has no marker support at all**, so the community's actual technique is "do two quick WOT blips after the event."

### rusEFI console
Its own author calls it "pretty plain" and explicitly not a replacement for third-party tuners. Concretely: gauges render with `setThresholdVisible(false)` so there are no warning/danger bands; the Log Viewer tab is commented out of the source; it requires a specific Java runtime. A 2013 feature request for a scrolling oscilloscope-style graph went several rounds of "I have no idea what to look at, without the context I am missing your point" before landing.

### Performance and scale
TunerStudio has an entire **Options → Performance** page dedicated to disabling gauge animation and enabling "lite mode," which tells you gauge rendering cost is a real problem on the hardware people actually use. OpenLogViewer's codebase is dominated by memory management, with user-facing strings like "Detected impending out-of-memory doom!" and an FPS counter in the chrome. MegaLogViewer's headline claim is navigating logs "hundreds of thousands of records long," which is a claim you only make because the naive implementation fails.

### Channel discovery
A Speeduino log has ~70 channels; a rusEFI log has hundreds. Speeduino's `.ini` mitigates this with `gaugeCategory` grouping; TunerStudio adds "Settings Search"; HyperTuner adds fuzzy search and a command palette. Everyone independently concluded that a flat channel list is unusable.

### Portability breaks silently
Community `.dash` files typically need output channels reassigned when moved between firmwares, because gauges bind to channel *names* that differ across ECUs, and there is no graceful degradation when a name doesn't resolve.

### Boot time
From rusEFI's own dash guidance: "a dash that takes thirty seconds to appear is a dash that is blank every time you start the car."

## 7. Distilled: what to actually build

The non-obvious ideas worth reimplementing, ranked:

1. **Every gauge limit is an expression, not a constant.** Redline follows the tune's own `rpmwarn` value. Units follow a preference. One dash works on every engine.
2. **Four thresholds, not two**: LowCritical / LowWarning / HighWarning / HighCritical. Oil pressure and battery voltage are dangerous on *both* ends.
3. **Peak-hold with a decay timer.** `ShowHistory` + `HistoricalPeakValue` + `HistoryDelay` (15 s default). You cannot watch a gauge at WOT; you need to see where it went afterward.
4. **`NeedleSmoothing` separate from the raw value**, and `PegLimits` so the needle clamps instead of wrapping.
5. **Explicit stale-data state** (`InvalidState` / `GoingDead`). A frozen number that looks live is the most dangerous failure mode in the whole category.
6. **`RunDemo` mode.** Design and test the dash with synthetic data, no car. Pair with something like `speeduino-serial-sim`.
7. **Relative 0..1 layout coordinates.** Same dash file on a 27" monitor and a 7" Pi screen.
8. **Task views, not just gauge pages.** Gauges + the relevant settings panel + the relevant table + a cell crosshair + a Burn button, saved as a named, shareable file.
9. **Synchronized cursor across stacked charts** (uPlot's `sync` key), X-only drag-zoom, Y-scales grouped by unit.
10. **The dashboard replays from the log.** Scrub the log, and gauges, indicators, and the table cell crosshair all animate. Everything you built for live monitoring becomes an analysis tool for free.
11. **Markers as first-class log data**, rendered as red ticks on the scrub bar, creatable by keypress, by screen double-tap, and by automated trigger with a text comment.
12. **Ring-buffer capture, save retroactively.** Never make the user pre-declare that they want to keep the data.
13. **Histogram / Table Generator with instant filter toggling**, and a **Z-Delta** mode that maps target-minus-actual error onto the tune's own axes. This is the single highest-leverage analysis view in the category.
14. **Filters named after physical reasons** (Accel Flag, ASE Flag, Overrun, Min CLT, Dead Lambda), not statistical ones.
15. **`isTrueFor(cond, seconds)` debounce** for every alarm, and a two-tier alert model: modal Global Warning vs corner Passive Message, plus audible.
16. **Indicator lamps carry a label in both states**, and where possible render the *reason* (`Fuel cut: <reason>`) rather than a generic light.
17. **Parse the log in a worker with a progress bar**; fuzzy-search the channel list; command palette for navigation.
18. **Single-file dashboards** with fonts and images embedded.
19. **Boot straight to the dash**, fullscreen, fast.
